modules.name: Eval Harness
modules.purpose: Scenario-first evaluation harness holding the platform's hard enablement gate, which has no off position for any account including the root. Stated purposes across 13 module records: §8.5 scenario-first harness + hard enablement gate (L2442); Band A harness enforcing the evaluation gate (L11662); evaluation scenario sets and evaluation runs (L21082); holds the scenario set gating every capability including the on-device deterministic layer and retrieval quality (L43714); the gate, the scenario set, harness behaviour and drift canary (L47795); eval posture view and eval-failure alerts (L55329); runs scenarios and suites, records pass/fail history, provides gate view and drift canary (L86042); drift canary re-runs the suite on cadence with a named owner (L98233); blocks enablement of any atom, agent or composed behaviour whose scenarios are pending or failing (L108748); scenario list, suite runner, gate view, drift canary panel (L108982). Declared feature set: FEAT-SA-05-01 (L43758), FEAT-SA-05-02 (L43765), FEAT-SA-05-03 (L43776) — the extract carries the identifiers but NOT their titles. Roles_allowed differs by record (see openQuestions).

hardGates.statement: No account, including the root, can disable the eval gate or sandbox-before-publish, and both render as ENFORCED in Settings.
Verdicts and their history cannot be edited or deleted by any account.
Every version of the on-device severity-classification table is re-evaluated before it distributes, and a failing version does not distribute. [applies_to MOD-SA-05 / MOD-SA-07]
With models unavailable, agent-behaviour scenarios render as unable-to-run rather than passing, and enablement remains blocked. (harness fails closed)

Enabling a capability with pending or failing evaluation scenarios is Explicitly prohibited for every account; the eval gate has no off position. [enforcement_point names MOD-SA-05 / §8.5.1 — this is the locked invariant]

There is no control anywhere on the Eval Harness screen that disables the gate, weakens a scenario's verdict, or marks a failing scenario as accepted, because none exists in the platform. [applies_to MOD-SA-05]
No agent, capability, or composed behaviour goes live without passing its evaluation scenarios. (hard enablement gate with no off position)
Specification gates are hard and always; the evaluation gate is hard and always including for the root account; the qualification gate is the only configurable gate.
No atom or agent can be enabled while any gating scenario is pending or failing, for any account including the root; the evaluation gate has no off position.

The evaluation gate sits BEFORE the approval cycle, not inside it; no approval path exists around the gate. An unavailable harness blocks rather than waives. [CONTRADICTED at L88306 — see openQuestions]
No account, including the Root Super Admin, can promote a capability that failed its evaluation scenarios.
No atom, agent, or composed agent can be enabled while any referenced scenario is pending or failing, for any account including the root.
No interface, application programming interface, configuration file, or database state exists that disables the evaluation gate.
The on-device severity-classification table is evaluated at every version before it distributes; a version that has not been evaluated cannot distribute.
Harness unavailability blocks enablement and never permits it. Failure to evaluate is failure to enable, never a bypass.

Enablement of an atom whose scenarios are pending or failing is refused at submit and again at apply, and both refusals are audit events. [applies_to MOD-SA-02; the double refusal is the MOD-SA-05 gate firing twice]

A failing evaluation cannot be enabled by any account; if the scenarios themselves are wrong, changing the scenarios is itself a submitted change requiring approval, so the gate cannot be weakened by quietly editing its own test.
An atom or agent whose scenarios are pending or failing cannot be enabled, and an enabled one whose evaluations start failing is flagged immediately.
No capability enables with pending or failing evaluation scenarios; disablement follows maker-checker; package-borne values are not retracted without a version.
A capability whose evaluation scenarios are pending or failing cannot be enabled for a tenant by any account.
No deployment path can enable a capability whose evaluation scenarios have not passed, and no account including the root can bypass the gate.
No capability becomes live by being deployed; enablement requires passing evaluation scenarios plus an audited submission and approval.
Any capability with pending or failing scenarios cannot be enabled, and the build cannot be promoted with such a capability marked enabled. [release pipeline gate]
The evaluation gate has no off position for any account; neither a Platform Engineer, nor an Admin, nor the Root Super Admin can proceed past it.
No artificial-intelligence health view exposes a confidence value used as a gate, and the drift canary's last result and named owner are always displayed.
No Studio action creates, alters, or removes an atom, a core agent definition, a memory store type, or an evaluation-harness rule.
A composed agent cannot act on any floor until the tenant approval chain, the evaluation gate, and platform review have all passed.
The Client Command Center cannot pause a run, stop a run, edit any record or configuration, create a Job or run, or override a specification or evaluation gate, for any role.
No override exists on any surface for any role for a specification gate or the evaluation gate.
All six invariants refuse every account including the root, through the interface and directly.
Absolute rule 11 — the six platform invariants bind every account including the root and have no off position and no approval path around them.
Retrieval quality is evaluated: retrieval behaviour is checked against scenario evaluations from day one, exactly like every other agent capability.
The on-device severity-classification table is a versioned artifact with scenario coverage, re-evaluated at every version before it distributes.
A control cannot be submitted unless its blast-radius preview asserts that no Severity 1 path, specification gate, evaluation gate, or on-device deterministic behaviour is touched.
No rollback of any kind removes an audit record, re-bases an in-flight run, or restores a capability that has not passed its evaluation scenarios.
A rollback may never restore a state in which a capability acts without passing its current evaluation scenarios, and may never re-base an in-flight run.
No version change, forward or backward, takes effect without the maker-checker approval discipline and the evaluation gate.
No mitigation weakens tenant isolation, the evaluation gate, the audit guarantee, or Quality-Manager-only release.
No deployment or migration may disable any of the six enforced invariants.
Manual fallback never substitutes for a control: it never replaces a specification gate, an evaluation gate, a qualification decision, an approval, a publication, or a Severity 1 hold.
No scheduled occurrence may publish an agent or composed behaviour that has not passed its evaluation scenarios.
In no storyboard does a failure of artificial intelligence cause a specification gate, evaluation gate, qualification gate, or Severity 1 hold to relax.

hardGates.statement: Traces are immutable once closed; no account can edit or delete one. (enforcement point: trace store)
No tenant surface exposes orchestrator internal reasoning; tenants receive a plain-language activity log and an evidence list only. (Tier-1-internal boundary)
A run whose trace or decision record cannot be written is recorded as failed or incomplete, never as a successful run. (enforcement point: trace close)
Replanning appears as a first-class trace event; raw reasoning never reaches a tenant surface; decision records persist for the record's full term while full traces are not retained beyond 24 months.
Full traces are retained 24 months; decision records persist for the full term of the operational record they explain.
No tenant surface renders raw reasoning internals, and no tenant-facing control implies they could be granted.
A derived decision record persists with the operational record for its full term, beyond the 24-month trace horizon.
Every gate outcome produces a decision record retained for the record's full term; raw reasoning is never exposed to a tenant.
Agent output that cannot be accompanied by a decision record is not delivered, because an agent contribution that cannot be explained afterwards must not influence a decision now.

Boundary three — the Client Command Center agent panel is NOT the trace viewer. Agent internals stay platform-internal; the panel renders the activity summary and evidence list only; no Command Center endpoint returns orchestrator reasoning internals.
An element classified PROV-1 that cannot produce an agent run identifier and a decision record fails closed to PROV-6.

No artificial-intelligence component participates in deviation triggering or classification. [enforcement point is TRACE INSPECTION asserting no model invocation precedes a deviation trigger — MOD-SA-06 is the evidence path for a platform-wide gate]
Archiving or removing an artificial-intelligence output from active use never deletes evidence, audit history, decision records, or the record of what the output did.
Partial output is quarantined rather than published: retained with its trace for engineering and audit, excluded from every official record, summary and export, never discarded.
Reaching the configured maximum replan count escalates to a human and never silently continues or silently stops. [replan is the first-class trace event MOD-SA-06 must render]

Every agent effect on state or on a worker is traceable either to a named pre-authorised policy object approved through the Studio approval chain, or to a named human gate decision in the Client Command Center.

(a) L9482: 'What happens when trace writing fails during an agent run?' — Client Decision Required, R&D recommendation, single option 'treat an untraceable agent run as a failed run and do not deliver its output'. (b) L47088: 'How is a capability section with no screen at V1 recorded' — impact '22 Super Admin screen register entries, of which only 21 render a screen at V1'. (c) L48736: 'Does a trace viewer screen exist at V1?'. (d) L116739 and L119098: 'Is the requirement register mirrored into an external requirements-management tool?' — a documentation-governance question with no relation to traces at all, adopted position option (a). Four decisions, one identifier. Nothing may cite DEC-TRACE-001 without naming the line.

CONTRADICTION — the evaluation gate's position relative to approval is stated both ways. L15993: 'The evaluation gate sits BEFORE the approval cycle, not inside it... no approval path exists around the gate.' L88306: 'The evaluation gate sits AFTER approval rather than before it, so an approved change that fails a scenario still does not ship.' Both are is_hard_gate=true. The outcome is the same (nothing ships) but the state machine and the screen ordering differ. Also L43255 (AC-SA-02-03) says the refusal fires TWICE — 'at submit and again at apply' — which is consistent with neither single ordering and may be the actual reconciliation.

CONTRADICTION — how many gates a composed agent passes. Three, in series: 'the tenant's approval chain, the evaluation gate, platform review' (L11989, restated AC-TIER-012 L12064). Order restated differently at L34137 (AC-STU-132): 'the evaluation gate, the tenant approval chain, and platform review, in that order'. Four: 'evaluation gate, Reviewer, Release Authority, platform review' (L88615). Three sources, three answers.

ROLE CONTRADICTION on the MOD-SA-05 suite runner — who may execute an eval run is stated four different ways: ROLE-PLAT-ENG + ROLE-PLAT-ROOT (L43706); Platform Engineer + Admin + Root Super Admin (L87338); Platform Engineer only (L108748 and L108982). The role matrix at L42713 explicitly says Admin may NOT do Band A mutation; at L42715 Support may NOT 'Run eval scenarios'. Yet the MOD-SA-05 module records at L21082, L43714, L86042 and L108982 all list Support in roles_allowed, and L108982 grants Support the Gate view. Best reading: Support and Admin get READ (gate view, drift canary panel) and Platform Engineer plus root get EXECUTE — but the source never says this in one place. Needs a decision before the permission matrix is coded.

ROLE CONTRADICTION on trace inspection — the MOD-SA-06 module records list ROLE-PLAT-ADMIN and ROLE-PLAT-SUP in roles_allowed (L21083, L43893), but the role matrix at L42713 says Admin may NOT 'Inspect a full trace through backend tooling — Band A inspection is engineering work' and at L42715 says Support may NOT 'Inspect a full trace'. Root and Platform Engineer are consistently permitted (L42712, L42714, L15955). The Read-only Auditor is Explicitly prohibited from reading platform-internal orchestrator traces (L16889).

OWNERSHIP CONTRADICTION on the derived decision record — L43904 assigns OBJ-SA-DECISIONRECORD to 'SURF-SA (derived); attaches to the operational record'; L13438 assigns the same object authoritative_owner_surface SURF-DOH. This decides which surface's team owns the write path and the full-term retention job.

RETENTION CONTRADICTION, already flagged in the source itself at L43837 — '§8.6.3 states full traces are retained 24 months while Part X states nothing is purged; reconciled as Derived Clarification that 24 months is the hot-retrievability horizon.' The reconciliation is DERIVED, not a SoW Fact, and the terminal state at L117972 ('traces persist longer than 24 months, a storage cost and not a compliance breach') and at L43839 ('tiers to lower-cost storage at 24 months, remaining retrievable') both support tiering-not-deletion — but SB-SCHED-29 (L102270) and SCHED-TRACE-RETENTION (L102417) describe traces REDUCING to decision records at 24 months, which reads as deletion. Confirm before writing the reaper.

OPEN DECISION blocking MOD-SA-05 delivery — DEC-CANARY-001 (L87338, L87340, L88902): drift-canary cadence and the action on canary failure are UNSET. Recommendation on record is option (b) per-class cadence (effect and detection-class atoms daily, read and retrieval atoms weekly) combined with option (c)'s provider-change event trigger. Impact as stated: 'Sets the maximum time a drifted capability can act on a floor undetected.' SB-SCHED-25 records the cadence as 'value TBD - Client Decision Required' (L102180). The drift canary panel (L108982) cannot render a cadence that has not been decided.

OPEN DECISION on the one path that could bypass the un-bypassable gate — DEC-EVALGOV-001 (L88398, L88400, L88416): how scenario changes are approved. Options are (a) all engineering class, (b) additions and strengthenings engineering class while removals and weakenings are critical class (recommended), (c) all critical class. Stated impact: 'Closes the one path by which the un-bypassable gate could be bypassed.' L65517 already asserts as a hard gate that 'changing the scenarios is itself a submitted change requiring approval' — but which approval class is undecided.

COUNT SCOPE — the numbers in this map are extracted-entry counts, not canonical inventory totals. source-reconciliation.json records platform totals of 1034 module entries, 725 workflow entries, 997 screen entries and 2964 business-rule entries across 36 chunks; these are extraction rows with heavy duplication across chunks, not distinct artefacts. Specifically: 13 module records mention MOD-SA-05 and 11 mention MOD-SA-06 (the same two modules re-described from different chapters); I report 8 screen entries for MOD-SA-05 and 5 for MOD-SA-06, which collapse to roughly 2 distinct screens (SCR-SA-06) and 0-1 (SCR-SA-07, disputed); I report 14 controls for MOD-SA-05 which collapse to roughly 4 distinct affordances (scenario list, suite runner, gate view, drift canary panel, per L108982). Do not publish any of these as a delivery count.

MOD-SA-06 HAS ZERO CONTROLS in the extract — no control record anywhere across the 36 chunks carries module_id MOD-SA-06. This is consistent with the backend-only-at-V1 scoping and is reported as a finding, not an omission. The two trace-adjacent controls that exist are tagged elsewhere: 'Open the trace viewer for a scenario run' is tagged mod:'Atom registry' (L65489) and 'view the activity log' is SURF-CC (L107697, explicitly 'no reasoning traces').

MODULE BOUNDARY DISPUTE on the emergency pause — L113588 places the 'Emergency pause control' at 'Super Admin module 5 (eval harness gate view panel 4)', root critical class. The screen register at L42803 assigns SCR-SA-11 'Emergency pause control' to MOD-SA-07. If both are true the pause is reachable from two modules; if only one, MOD-SA-05's gate view has either three or four panels. L108982 enumerates exactly four MOD-SA-05 panels and emergency pause is not among them (scenario list, suite runner, gate view, drift canary panel).

SCREEN REGISTER COLLISION — two Super Admin screen registers use the SCR-SA-NN namespace with different assignments. L42793-42810: SCR-SA-01 Overview, 02 Atom registry, 03 Agent roster, 04 Composed-agent review, 05 Memory. L48730-48740: SCR-SA-01 Console sign-in, 02 Overview, 03 Atom registry, 04 Agents and composed-agent review, 05 Memory. The two registers happen to AGREE on SCR-SA-06 (eval harness, MOD-SA-05), SCR-SA-07 (trace, MOD-SA-06) and SCR-SA-08 (Platform Settings), so this map is unaffected — but a third naming (SCR-SA-EVALS and SCR-SA-EVALGATE at L87376) splits the eval harness into TWO screens where the other two registers show one. Whether the harness is one screen with four panels or two screens is unresolved.

SCHEDULER COUNT CONTRADICTION touching the drift canary — L9993 names FOUR platform schedulers including the drift canary; L99594 says 'Three named platform schedulers in the source: run auto-close, storage tiering and anonymisation, the drift canary' which names four items while claiming three. The drift canary's scheduler identity is constrained at L99235: the AI scheduler identity is 'narrowed to the evaluation harness for the drift canary' and may only view its own definitions, occurrences and receipts — all other twenty operations Explicitly prohibited.

MOD-SA-05 SCOPE UNSETTLED — what the gate actually covers is stated at different widths. L43714: the scenario set gates every capability 'including the on-device deterministic layer and retrieval quality'. L108878: 'atoms, agents, composed agents, retrieval, on-device deterministic layer'. L88398: 'atoms, agents, composed agents and the on-device severity table'. L4616: applies_to 'SURF-SA, SURF-STU, SURF-FL'. Retrieval quality is confirmed separately at L96235. The severity-classification table gate (AC-SA-05-06, L43804) is shared with MOD-SA-07 — build ownership of that re-evaluation-before-distribution path is not assigned to one module.

SCENARIO COUNT is illustrative, never a commitment, and the source says so — 'roughly fifty' scenarios is labelled '(illustrative, never a delivery commitment)' at L43663 and 'illustrative and not a committed count' at L87334. What IS enumerated is 2 named seed scenarios plus 6 platform scenarios = 8, listed in order at L87334. The seed torque figures (51 Nm against a 47 Nm upper limit) are flagged at L86493 as 'a platform fixture, NOT the Bright Bikes specification'. A separate sizing of '20-50 tasks per agent' appears at L120406 and a '50 scenarios' deterministic subset for the differential replay harness at L89160 — three different fifties.

FAILURE CONTRACTS bind both modules and are not optional. MOD-SA-05: FB-SA-06 (L42863) harness unavailable -> retry -> refuse enablement -> 'the gate fails closed and has no off position'; FB-ENG-001 (L15976) 'an unavailable gate blocks rather than waives'; FB-SA-001 (L11687) 'If the evaluation harness is unavailable, nothing agentic may be published — that is the gate working'; FB-007 (L110827) on return the drift canary runs IMMEDIATELY rather than waiting for cadence and every capability enabled during the gap is re-verified; FAIL-AI-37/38 (L90509, L90510); FB-SA-08 (L42865) drift-canary scheduler misfire. MOD-SA-06: FB-AI-01 (L74495) trace store unavailable -> decision record written and trace marked unavailable -> if neither can be written the output is not delivered; FB-AI-12 (L87522) retry the trace write, then the run terminates as a recorded failure, 'a trace gap explicitly recorded as a gap rather than silently absent'; FAIL-AI-59 (L90733) trace/decision-record/operational-record reconciliation mismatch freezes reconciliation and alters no record until explained. FB-AI-11 and FB-AI-12 appear again at L88926-88927 as bare identifiers with every contract field null — an extraction hole, or an unwritten contract in the source.

openQuestions: SCREEN NUMBERING IS SELF-CONTRADICTORY ACROSS TWO REGISTERS. The §23 register (L42808-L42810 and L45160/L45273/L45385) numbers these SCR-SA-16 (metrics), SCR-SA-17 (tiers), SCR-SA-18 (usage). A second register at L48742-L48744 numbers the same three screens SCR-SA-13, SCR-SA-14, SCR-SA-15 — and in that register SCR-SA-16 is 'Devices and fleet' (L48745), SCR-SA-17 is 'Platform notifications' (L48746), SCR-SA-18 is 'Support access sessions' (L48747). The identifier-index confirms the collision: SCR-SA-16 -> [42808, 45160, 48745]; SCR-SA-17 -> [42809, 45273, 48746]; SCR-SA-18 -> [42810, 42971, 45385]. The build MUST pick one numbering scheme and record the decision; the source does not.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA ARE MISSING FROM THE EXTRACT, NOT FROM THE SOURCE. identifier-index shows AC-SA-10-01 through AC-SA-10-06 all at L45230, AC-SA-11-01 through AC-SA-11-06 all at L45342, and AC-SA-12-01 through AC-SA-12-07 all at L45456. The extract's business_rules arrays carry only AC-SA-10-02/-03/-04, AC-SA-11-01/-02/-03/-04/-06, and AC-SA-12-02/-03/-04/-07. AC-SA-10-01, AC-SA-10-05, AC-SA-10-06, AC-SA-11-05, AC-SA-12-01, AC-SA-12-05 and AC-SA-12-06 exist in the frozen source but their statements are NOT in this extract. Seven acceptance criteria must be re-read from the source before build.

THE FIFTEEN NAMED PER-TENANT MEASURES ARE NEVER ENUMERATED. L45134 states the count (15 measures, applies_to MOD-SA-10) and L107350 says they render as tiles with value, comparison window and completeness indicator, but no state_vocabulary or list anywhere in the 36 chunks names them. Five functions FUNC-SA-10-01-A1..E1 (L45211-L45219) sit under FEAT-SA-10-01 (L45209) — five functions for fifteen measures, so the mapping is not one-to-one and is unstated. MOD-SA-10 cannot be built from this extract alone.

TIER RECORD STATE VOCABULARY IS STATED FOUR DIFFERENT WAYS. OBJ-SA-TIER L45292: draft / pending root approval / published / superseded (four states, matches OBJ-003 at L7673). OBJ-unnumbered-TIER L56912: draft / published (two). OBJ-TIER L21282: version created / published (two). OBJ-TIER L2195: versioned / approvable (not a lifecycle at all). OBJ-TIER L61321: unassigned / Growth (a tenant's assigned value, not a record lifecycle). Build the four-state version (it is the only one anchored to a per-module §8.11 body) and flag the divergence.

GROWTH TIER CEILING: 199 OR 200? The tier band vocabulary says Growth is 100-199 Worker-Shifts/month and Enterprise 200+ (L2195, L45244). Worked examples consistently use 199 as the Growth ceiling (L26903 '80 against 199'; L57349 '80 consumed carried against the new 199'; L72062 'new ceiling of 199'; L26900 'Bright Bikes, Growth tier, ceiling 199'). But the MOD-SA-12 illustrative example at L45387 uses a 200 ceiling ('160 of 200' at 80 percent, '205' entering burst). The source is inconsistent about whether the allocation ceiling equals the band's upper bound.

USAGE LADDER VOCABULARY IS RESTATED SIX TIMES WITH DIFFERENT SHAPES. L45405 (five states, includes an explicit 'under 80 percent'), L57283 (four rungs with behaviours), L2197 (four rungs), L4648 (five bands 'below 80 / 80 / 100 / burst / above 125'), L117903 (four: 80 / 100 / 125 / burst entry), L26875 (four, snake_case, tenant-side MOD-DOH-01). The thresholds 80/100/125 and burst are consistent everywhere; the STATE NAMES and whether a below-80 state is modelled are not. Pick one and record it.

LEDGER EXPORT MECHANISM IS UNDECIDED — DEC-USAGE-001 (L96587). Options: (a) operator-initiated console export only at V1 (adopted working position), (b) operator export plus a scheduled drop to a client-controlled destination, (c) a full machine-to-machine feed. A related contradiction is recorded at L96587: §8.7.1 places outbound data delivery in the second version while §8.12.4 / §4.11.5 place the export at V1. The export control at L45385 must ship as (a) unless the client rules otherwise.

OBJ-SA-LEDGEREVENT AND OBJ-SA-OVERRIDE AND OBJ-SA-DISTRIBUTION HAVE NO STATE VOCABULARY. Their states arrays at L45404, L45292 and L45179 are empty. For the ledger event a competing statement at L7692 (OBJ-004 Usage Ledger Entry) DOES give recorded / aggregated / exported. For the override flag and the comparative distribution the source is simply silent — the implementation must not invent a lifecycle for either.

MOD-SA-10 HAS NO MUTATING CONTROL ANYWHERE IN THE EXTRACT. The only two controls found (L107350) are both read/navigate onward actions from a metric tile, and the source explicitly calls them 'exactly two onward actions'. Metrics and distributions are 'derived, never authored' (L45179). Treat the absence as designed, not as a gap — but note that no refresh, no recompute and no export control is stated for MOD-SA-10 at all.

MOD-SA-11 HAS EXACTLY ONE CONTROL WITH AN EXPLICIT module_id — the mandatory grandfathering declaration (L45273). Draft, submit, approve, publish, assign, and supersede are all described as workflow steps (L45248, L15838) and as critical-class approvals (L45342, L15360), but no extract entry carries them as labelled controls with allowed_roles. Roles must be derived from the workflow actors (Admin drafts, Root Super Admin approves) and from AC-SA-11-02.

PER-TENANT OVERRIDE VS TIER ENTITLEMENT PRECEDENCE IS OPEN — DEC-FEAT-004 (L54665, L94229 context). Interim rule: the more restrictive state applies and the ambiguity is named (AC-WF-FEAT-002-03, L54672; fallback FB-FEAT-002 at L54668). The implementation may not guess a winner. This directly gates WF-FEAT-002 (L54658), which the source binds to MOD-SA-11.

AUTOMATIC TIER DOWNGRADE IS PERMANENTLY REJECTED (P12), as is automatic suspension release on payment (P13) — recorded in the closed_action_sets of registries/generated/source-reconciliation.json ('Permanently rejected automations — FOUR'). The downgrade queue (L45103, L72062, L72066) must be advanced by an operator act, not by a scheduler. DEC-SUSP-001 (L96507) separately records the contradiction that §8.9.2 and Part IX make soft-suspension exit automatic on payment while §4.2.4 makes it an operator signal, with the operator signal adopted as the working position.

MODULE ROLE LISTS DISAGREE ACROSS SIX RESTATEMENTS. For all three modules, L45164/L45277/L45389 give four console roles (Root, Admin, Platform Engineer, Support); L21087-L21089 give three (Root, Admin, Support); L11667-L11669 give two (Root, Admin); L4623 and L57277 and L60867 and L99438 give Admin only for MOD-SA-12; L57372 gives Admin + Root for MOD-SA-10. L42744-L42746 give all four as ROLE-PLAT-* identifiers. The only consistent negative is L44813: no tenant role may reach MOD-SA-10, -11 or -12. Resolve the read/write split per role before building the permission matrix.

MODULE-BODY LINE SPANS DO NOT CONTAIN THEIR OWN WORKFLOWS. In CHK-014 the tier-publication workflow sits at L45248 (inside MOD-SA-10's span L45164-L45276) and the usage-metering workflow at L45360 (inside MOD-SA-11's span L45277-L45388). Any tooling that assigns workflows to modules by line proximity will mis-assign both. Assignment in this map is by name and topic; that method is stated, not inferred.

DEC-REPORT-001 (L45138) — the identities of the five standard report data sets are marked 'Not stated in the source' at the head of the MOD-SA-10 section, yet three other chunks DO enumerate five sets (L9266, L29884, L38261) and all three include 'tier-allocation consumption trend' / 'Allocation consumption trend', which reads on MOD-SA-12's ledger. The open decision and the enumerations contradict each other.

DEC-SCHED-001..010 ARE ALL OPEN AND THE IDENTIFIERS THEMSELVES COLLIDE (recorded in source-reconciliation residual_contradictions, and at L99430, L99444). SCHED-USAGE-LADDER (L102029, L102031) is the scheduled occurrence that drives the MOD-SA-12 ladder; its misfire policy, duplicate-execution guard (DEC-SCHED-003, L117957) and authoritative clock (DEC-SCHED-002, L117956) are all undecided. WF-USAGE-LADDER's guarantee that 'a threshold event fires once per crossing, not once per evaluation' (L117965) has no decided idempotency mechanism behind it.

DEC-ANON-001 (L97583) is unresolved and touches MOD-SA-10's comparative aggregates indirectly: the no-purge model claims nothing ceases to exist while anonymisation permanently destroys a category of information. The anonymisation machinery itself is owned by MOD-SA-17, not by these three modules (controls at L97560, screens at L97555), so do not build de-anonymisation or reversal affordances into the metrics module.

A SECOND FEATURE-NUMBERING SCHEME EXISTS AND IS NOT IN THE EXTRACT BODY. identifier-index shows FEAT-SA-1001/1002/1003 (L47810-L47812), FEAT-SA-1101/1102/1103 (L47813-L47815) and FEAT-SA-1201/1202/1203 (L47816-L47818) alongside the hyphenated FEAT-SA-10-01..10-03 (L45209/L45220/L45223), FEAT-SA-11-01..11-04 (L45322/L45327/L45330/L45336) and FEAT-SA-12-01..12-04 (L45436/L45440/L45446/L45449). Note the count mismatch: three flat-numbered features versus four hyphenated ones for both MOD-SA-11 and MOD-SA-12. The chunk containing L47810-L47818 stops its module extraction at MOD-SA-07 (L47801), so the mapping between the two schemes is not recoverable from this extract.

value.cluster: SURF-SA (Super Admin platform console) — MOD-SA-08 Console Users, Roles and Change Approvals; MOD-SA-09 Tenants, Lifecycle and Pilots; MOD-SA-19 The Tenant-Configuration Registry. Counts below are extracted-entry counts from registries/raw/extract/CHK-0NN.json (36 chunks), NOT canonical blueprint inventory totals. Extract-wide totals for scale: 1034 module entries, 725 workflow entries, 997 screen entries, 759 control entries, 685 object entries, 2964 business_rules of which 2818 carry is_hard_gate:true, 1190 state_vocabularies, 566 contradictions (registries/generated/source-reconciliation.json, totals block). Of 377 extracted workflow entries whose surfaces_touched includes SURF-SA, the three modules below account for the entries listed here; the remainder belong to the other 16 SURF-SA modules.

modules.name: Console Users, Roles and Change Approvals
modules.purpose: Holds the console access model — exactly one root account and four fixed platform roles (ROLE-PLAT-ROOT, ROLE-PLAT-ADMIN, ROLE-PLAT-ENG, ROLE-PLAT-SUP) — plus the maker-checker and critical-class approval discipline governing every platform change (L44778, L2442 '§8.8; maker-checker, root-only actions and the critical change class', L11665 'Band B: console accounts, role grants and the maker-checker approval cycle', L21085, L42742, L98236, L116399). Root-only acts: console account creation, role assignment, critical-class approval (L44711 roles_rules ROLE-PLAT-ROOT, governing_decision DEC-ROOT-001). The extract names 13 FUNC-SA-08-* function ids at L44778 (FUNC-SA-08-01-A1/A2/A3, -02-A1/B1, -03-A1/A2/B1, -04-A1/A2/A3, -05-A1/A2) spanning §8.8.1–§8.8.5, and a separate id family at L60863 (FUNC-SA-ACCOUNT-ACTIVATE, FUNC-SA-ROLE-SET, FUNC-SA-ROLE-CHANGE-LIVE, FUNC-SA-ACCOUNT-DISABLE, FUNC-SA-OFFBOARD-CONSOLE, FUNC-SA-IDENTITY-CONTROL) and another at L55552 (FUNC-SA-BACKEND-CREATE, FUNC-SA-ROLE-SET, FUNC-SA-DECIDE-CRITICAL, FUNC-SA-ACCOUNT-DISABLE, FUNC-SA-OFFBOARD-CONSOLE) — three non-identical function-id vocabularies for the same module. Key numerics: exactly 1 root account (L44705, L55527); approval requests carry 9 stated fields (L44881); 10 critical-class actions route to root (L44880), though the enumeration as written lists 11 items (L55942); TEST-RBAC-302 expects 30 audited denials = 10 critical actions x 3 non-root roles (L21218).

hardGates.statement: The platform is provisioned with exactly one Super Admin account, created through the backend at platform commissioning and never through any user interface. Enforcement: backend commissioning; no user interface path exists.
Roles are fixed at V1 with no custom role authoring; custom roles are roadmap. Enforcement: Roles pane / console role model.
A Platform Engineer's change is submitted and takes effect only when an Admin approves it (maker-checker). Enforcement: approval queue.

An approved change destined for a device becomes a command and waits; the queue shows the change applied at the platform and the fleet view shows the command's exact state at each device — two deliberately different facts, never conflated.
Console has no offline mode; no approval is cached or applied from a stale client, which is a segregation-of-duties control as much as a technical one.
Exactly one root account exists, and no user interface path creates a second.
No account can approve its own submission.
All ten critical-class actions route to the root, and an Admin cannot approve any of them.
Approval requests carry all nine stated fields and commit under the one-transaction guarantee.
Composed-agent reviews and tier publications appear in the same queue under their own classes, and no parallel decision queue exists.
The implementation authoring role can author and submit inside a tenant workspace but can never approve or release, and its provisioning and revocation appear in both audit streams.
The live per-module roles matrix contains no blank cell — every cell carries an explicit status from the closed set. Enforcement: SCR-SA-12 Roles pane rendering.
No account other than the Root Super Admin can create a console account or assign a console role, under any configuration. Enforcement: console Users pane.
The six enforced invariants present no off control to any account, and a direct application programming interface attempt to disable one denies and is audited.
Critical-class requests never auto-approve, expire silently, or apply without a recorded root decision; they wait and re-notify. Enforcement: approval queue aging re-notification.

There is no self-registration, no password-only path, and no role-escalation path except the root acting. Account provisioning events, including the backend creation of the root itself, are audit events. Enforcement: server-side refusal on every endpoint.

Mutating administrative changes follow maker-checker: a Platform Engineer's change takes effect only when an Admin approves it; user creation and role changes are root-only; the critical class escalates to the root. Enforcement: approval queue routing by change class.
Exactly one root exists. No user interface creates a root. An action that cannot be audited does not happen — the audit event fails, the account must not exist.
All six invariants are unchangeable by the root; server-side refusal is independent of interface state.
Custom console roles cannot be created at V1; roles are fixed at four.
No Platform Engineer change applies without an Admin approval; self-approval is impossible. Enforcement: server-side queue routing regardless of path used.
Band B actions auto-apply and are audited; every tenant-visible act mirrors — no unmirrored platform-side act against a tenant persists, because Platform Access History is a tenant right.
All ten critical actions route to the root; class cannot be downgraded; classification sits in the platform rather than the operator's hands.
No critical request auto-approves and no critical request expires; the request stays pending and visible forever rather than expiring; the aging itself is the signal.
De-escalation applies before escalation on any combined role change, so no union state of the two role sets exists at any moment.
The root cannot be disabled; no pending item auto-resolves on disablement.
Roles are re-assigned explicitly, never restored silently, mirroring the worker re-employment rule; re-enable is root-only.
No console account exists that the root did not create; every self-registration attempt is refused server-side on every path and audited.
Effective capability never exceeds assigned role; escalation attempts, including approving one's own role change, are audited and surfaced.
The root-account count is exactly one at all times; promotion to root is impossible; backend creation of a second root is refused. Enforcement: uniqueness constraint with continuous reconciliation.
Tenant operations are unaffected by root unavailability; no critical action is performed without root approval regardless of urgency; no second root is created as a workaround.
Multi-factor authentication is never disabled to restore access; the succession path is the only alternative.
Every action by a compromised account is enumerable from the audit log and no audit history can be deleted; the log is append-only and immutable.
Urgency never bypasses maker-checker or the critical class; no ambient access is opened during an incident.
The live matrix, stored assignments, and audit history must agree before an attestation is issued; no tenant operational content leaves through the export path.

Queue drain follows submission order with critical items first; stale device commands are superseded rather than replayed; a reconciliation statement is produced and audited; tenant operations are unaffected throughout.
No user-interface path creates a Super Admin account; the count of root accounts is exactly one at all times.
A Platform Engineer's mutating change never applies on submission and is visibly pending until an Admin approves it.
No console role, including the root, can disable any of the six ENFORCED platform invariants.
Mutating changes ride maker-checker, with ten named critical-class actions requiring root approval. Enforcement: approval queue SCR-SA-10.
No ambient browsing exists anywhere on the console; record-level content requires one of the three named access classes.

hardGates.statement: No public self-signup path exists; every tenant is created by the client's platform team. Onboarding is invitation-driven.
Tenant creation provisions an isolated data space, and isolation is architectural rather than a permission setting.
Soft suspension blocks master-data writes while runs continue to be created, scheduled, and executed. Enforcement: authorisation layer.
Hard suspension permits the enumerated completion pipeline and blocks all new runs.
Compliance suspension blocks all logins immediately, stops in-flight runs, and locks devices at next contact with the fixed message. Enforcement: authorisation layer plus command channel.
The only platform-side entry into a compliance-suspended tenant is the dual-authorised compliance-emergency path.
A device lock is never rendered as applied before the device acknowledges it.
Pilot conversion preserves the tenant identifier and requires no re-onboarding.
Downgrades never execute mid-cycle and carry a visible pending-downgrade status, queued behind consumption fit.
Tenant groups have no operational behaviour and are never visible in any tenant surface.
No operational action of any kind can be taken from the tenant detail page by any console role — visibility, not intervention. Enforcement: tenant detail page Operations tab.
None of the suspension notifications enforces the suspension; the suspension is enforced by the authorisation layer and, on devices, by the applied command.
The worker-facing compliance message is fixed: 'Operation suspended. Contact your supervisor. Your work has been saved.' Enforcement: Frontline Worker Application device string.
No tenant becomes reachable before its isolated data space is confirmed provisioned. Enforcement: provisioning state machine.
Exactly one Tenant Admin is seeded per tenant by the platform side; thereafter user management is tenant-administered.

Soft blocks master-data writes and configuration edits while operations continue; recertification stays open; hard permits the enumerated completion pipeline and no new runs; under soft and hard no worker-facing message appears.
The soft exit is an explicit operator signal in the Super Admin platform console, and no tenant-state transition anywhere keys on a payment event.

Compliance suspension requires root approval; the worker-facing message matches the source string verbatim; no device is reported as locked before it confirms; only the compliance-emergency path enters a compliance-suspended tenant.
The activation control is unavailable until every mandatory provisioning step carries a committed success event in the tenant's audit stream.
Every provisioning step, retry, rollback and activation commits its audit event in the same transaction as the change itself.

Seeding the first Tenant Admin is refused while the isolated data space is unconfirmed, with the outstanding step named; an out-of-order seeding request is rejected as an ordering violation and writes a rejection event.
The tenant-group label is an internal label of the client's team only, with no operational behaviour, and is absent from every response served to any tenant-facing surface.
All six provisioning steps are idempotent: a repeated request produces no second data space, no second account and no second invitation record.
Authoring under an expired implementation authoring capacity is denied at request time regardless of the grant record's stored state, so the safe outcome does not depend on a background process.

Sending is not delivery; delivery is not opening; opening is not acknowledgement; acknowledgement is not the business action. The console must never display 'invitation sent' as though it were 'administrator active'.
A notification must never be the only mechanism enforcing an authorisation; the invitation does not grant authority by being received.
An expired, revoked or superseded invitation cannot activate an account.
A failed or abandoned identity proof leaves no partially activated account and no usable credential material.
Requesting an invitation status without an authenticated console session returns no information about whether the account exists.
An invitation is single-use: a second use of the same link after activation is refused.
Under hard suspension no new version may be adopted because that is a configuration change; a worker never clears their own block. Enforcement: server state validation.

hardGates.statement: Every write path, tenant-side and platform-side, lands at the registry, and no bypass exists.

A looser-than-floor value is rejected at the point of entry with the bound stated and is not stored — never accepted and logged. Enforcement: registry bound validation against the platform floor register.
All seventeen governed settings are present and each has a floor-register bound. Enforcement: registry schema.
Current-value changes platform-side are Admin actions, default changes are engineering-class, and bound changes are critical-class. Enforcement: maker-checker class routing.
Tightening a bound surfaces non-conforming values rather than rewriting them. Enforcement: conformance report.

Tenants may only make the platform stricter than default and never looser than the platform floor, with rejection rather than logging; seven platform-fixed items are named. Enforcement: tenant-configuration registry (MOD-SA-19), single enforcement point; applies to all five surfaces, every role including the root.
An out-of-bound tenant configuration value fails the write and returns the bound; it is never accepted and logged. Enforcement: Tenant-Configuration Registry.
A looser-than-floor value is rejected and not written; the rejection states the bound. Verification: TEST-TA-002.
Where a bound cannot be read, the change is refused rather than applied. Verification: TEST-TA-004.

Every value is validated against the Super Admin tenant-configuration registry: the platform rejects, rather than logs, any value looser than the platform floor. Tenants tighten; they never loosen. Enforcement: tenant administration area write path; FB-DOH-WRITE-002.
A looser-than-floor value is rejected at entry with the bound stated and is not persisted. Enforcement: platform floor register.
A package-borne configuration change is never displayed as in force on a device before that device confirms the package version.

A looser-than-floor value is rejected at entry; configuration writes are blocked under soft suspension while run creation continues; no package-borne change is shown as in force before device acknowledgement.
The tenant-configuration registry rejects an out-of-bound value at entry with the bound stated, and never accepts and logs it.

openQuestions: Method disclosure — how each workflow was attributed. EXACT (module entry names the workflow id in key_functions): MOD-SA-08 ← 'WF-ROLE-001 to WF-ROLE-045' (L55552); MOD-SA-09 ← WF-TEN-001, WF-TEN-002 (L52395) and WF-PLT-004, WF-PLT-005 (L55108); MOD-SA-19 ← WF-FEAT-002 (L54658). All other workflows listed were attributed by line proximity to the module's section anchors and by subject-name match, NOT by an explicit module_id field — the workflow records in registries/raw/extract carry no module_id at all. Screens and controls were matched exactly on their module_id field.

MOD-SA-08 is credited with the entire WF-ROLE-001..045 family at L55552, but WF-ROLE-022 to WF-ROLE-030 (support sessions, compliance-emergency path, JBS access grants) are subject-matter of MOD-SA-15 Support Access and MOD-SA-16 JBS Access, both named in the same module set at L4567. The source does not say whether these nine workflows are built under MOD-SA-08 or under MOD-SA-15/16. Build ownership must be decided before work is split.

Numbered acceptance-criteria sequences are incomplete in the extract, and the gaps are not marked as absent-by-design. AC-SA-08 has 01, 05, 06, 07, 08, 09, 10, 12 (L44875–L44886) — 02, 03, 04, 11 are missing. AC-SA-09 has 01–06, 08, 10–14 (L45092–L45105) — 07 and 09 are missing. AC-SA-19 has 02, 03, 05, 07, 09 (all at L46318) — 01, 04, 06, 08 are missing. Either the extractor dropped them or the source skips numbers; the registries cannot tell you which. Do not treat the listed gates as the complete gate set for these modules.

SCR-SA screen numbering is not stable across the source. SCR-SA-12 is 'Console users pane and roles matrix pane' at L42804 and L44774, but 'Tenant detail' at L48741. The registry screen is SCR-SA-26 at L42818/L46246 and SCR-SA-22 at L48751; the tenant list is SCR-SA-14 at L42806/L44984 and SCR-SA-11 at L48740; the approval queue is SCR-SA-13 at L42805/L44774 and SCR-SA-10 at L48739. Two independent screen-numbering schemes exist. Pick one and record the mapping before any screen id is used as a build key.

MOD-SA-09 tenant detail page tab count is self-contradictory in the source: §8.9.6 prose asserts eight tabs while the named groupings are seven — Overview, Operations, Agents, Memory, Devices, Metrics, Logs and Audit — with the eighth produced only by splitting 'Logs and Audit' into two (L45070, L45126, L52383). Recorded as a Derived Clarification with no governing decision; the blueprint says the difference is cosmetic and affects no behaviour.

DEC-SUSP-001 (L44927): soft-suspension exit is stated three incompatible ways — §4.2.4 operator signal, §8.9.2 'Automatic on payment', Part IX 'soft clears on payment' — while §4.2.1 and §8.12 state there is no payment integration on the platform. Adopted working position is option (c): operator-signal exit built at V1, inbound payment path left open and unbuilt. Status: adopted 2026-08-14, ratification still owed by the client's platform team. AC-WF-PLT-004-05 (L55123) enforces the operator-signal reading.

DEC-MSG-001 (L44923): the worker-facing compliance-suspension string differs between §4.2.3 ('Operation suspended. Contact your supervisor. Your work has been saved.') and §8.9.2 ('Operation suspended — your work has been saved.'). Recorded as a drafting inconsistency, not behavioural, but the string is a hard gate (L44923) and ships in the Frontline application — one wording must be chosen.

The critical class is described as 'the ten named critical actions' but the enumeration as written lists eleven items (L55942): tier publication, compliance suspension, all-tenant broadcast, device wipe, emergency pause, emergency resume, erasure and archival execution, retention-value changes, legal-hold place and release, severity-catalog changes, floor-register changes. Pause and resume are named separately. AC-SA-08-06 (L44880) and AC-WF-ROLE-018-01 (L55969) both say 'ten'. The routing table cannot be built until the count is settled.

Console account disablement authority is undecided (L55560): the permission matrix marks Admin disablement 'Client Decision Required — the source names create, role assignment, disable and last-activity review in one pane without splitting authority', while WF-ROLE-032 (L56278) and WF-ROLE-033 (L56301) and the extracted control at L55552 all treat disable and re-enable as root-only. No governing decision id is recorded.

Root self-approval versus creator-is-never-approver (L21146, L55989, governing decisions DEC-ROOTSOD-001 and DEC-ROOTSUCC-001): §8.8.1/§8.8.3 make the root the sole approver of the critical class gated by nothing but the invariants, while §3.5, §4.5.2 and §5.11.1 make creator-is-never-approver absolute, and AC-SA-08-05 (L44879) states flatly that no account can approve its own submission. The blueprint records the root exception as an Assumption with the single-point concentration noted, not as a resolved rule.

DEC-ROOTSUCC-001 is open, TBD Client Decision Required (L56417): how root custody is recovered when the sole root is unavailable. Options recorded: documented backend re-provisioning under dual custody; a sealed break-glass credential held by the client; a standby root which would violate the exactly-one rule. WF-ROLE-038's fallback of backend re-provisioning is flagged as neither described nor forbidden by the source, while AC-WF-ROLE-037-01 (L56398) refuses backend creation of a second root. Impact as recorded: root loss simultaneously freezes compliance suspension, device wipe, emergency pause, retention changes, legal hold, severity-catalog changes and floor changes.

DEC-FEAT-001 (L21098, L46211, L54664): feature and atom enablement is a Platform Engineer change requiring Admin approval under §8.2.2 but an Admin action under §8.19. The two readings assign different makers to the same act, and MOD-SA-19's AC-SA-19-07 (L46318) depends on the answer for its class routing.

DEC-FEAT-004 (L54665): a per-tenant override flag and the tier entitlement can contradict each other and the precedence rule is undecided. The blueprint states explicitly that the implementation may not guess; AC-WF-FEAT-002-03 (L54672) applies the more restrictive of the two states as an interim rule only.

MOD-SA-19's seventeen governed settings are asserted as a count (L46308) and made a hard gate (AC-SA-19-05, L46318), but the extract nowhere enumerates all seventeen. Only three are individually visible: record-finish window (default 48h, bounds 24h to 7 days, L46207/L11797), qualification-expiry warning schedule (14/7/1/0 days, earlier only, L46207), and the non-payment suspension thresholds (30/60 days, L44919/L44920). Fourteen settings and every one of their bounds must be sourced before the registry schema can be built.

MOD-SA-19 has exactly ONE extracted actionable control across all 36 chunks — the conformance panel at L46246 (Root Super Admin, Admin, Platform Engineer, Support). The registry's own write, edit, revert-to-default and bound-change controls are not present as control entries anywhere, although AC-SA-19-07 (L46318) presupposes them. This is a genuine hole in the mapped surface, not a module with few controls by design.

MOD-SA-19's roles_allowed varies materially by chunk with no reconciliation: Root Super Admin only (L11676); Admin only (L2442); Admin + Platform Engineer + Root + Tenant Admin (L4630); all four console roles (L21096, L42753); all four plus 'Tenant Admin (own operational settings, tenant-side)' (L46250); Root + Admin + 'Tenant Admin (as subject)' (L60874); and an empty array (L98247). The read/write split by role is not determinable from the registries.

Several MOD-SA-08/09/19 objects carry empty state arrays in the extract with no statement that they are stateless: OBJ-SA-ROLEASSIGN (L44793), OBJ-SA-TENANTSTATE and OBJ-SA-GROUP (L45003), OBJ-SA-REGISTRY (L46265), OBJ-CONFIG-REGISTRY (L2173), OBJ-SA-OVERRIDE (L45292), OBJ-SA-ENABLEMENT (L43177). Whether these are genuinely stateless records or extraction gaps is not stated.

The tenant object has at least eight non-identical state vocabularies across chunks (L45003, L2141, L3914, L7635, L55122, L75159, L71219, L117352, L81024, L98253), differing in whether compliance suspension, pilot, invited, pending-downgrade and the archive/offboarding states are members, and differing in casing convention. The fifteen-state SEQ-031/032 list at L71219 is never reconciled against the eight-state OBJ-SA-TENANT at L45003. One canonical tenant state machine must be declared before any state column is persisted.

The approval-request state machine has two irreconcilable forms: the four-state pending/approved/returned/applied vocabulary repeated at L21050, L23750, L44794, L55895 and L104797, and the nine-state Drafting/Pending/Returned/Declined/Approved/Applied/Mirrored/Commanded/Acknowledged machine at L104816, plus two extra failure states approved-not-applied and approved-not-executed at L55897 and a 'declined' state at L104797. DEC-HO-SUPGRANT-001 (L23773): the source does not state whether a support session is opened self-service by Support against a valid ticket or requires an Admin grant per session or per tenant. This gates WF-ROLE-022 (L56054), which the extract assigns to MOD-SA-08.

hardGates.statement: Every aggregate view renders an as-of timestamp, and a degraded aggregate renders as stale-with-age or unavailable, never as zero and never blank. (enforcement: aggregation layer rendering; applies to SURF-SA)
No console screen outside a named access session renders record-level operational content for any tenant. (enforcement: three-layer data-access model)

The console being wholly unavailable causes no change to deterministic on-device safety behaviour, agent enablement, or audit commitment on any tenant surface. (enforcement: control plane vs runtime separation)
No tenant role can authenticate to the Super Admin platform console under any configuration, including during a support session, a compliance-emergency session, or a JBS grant.

Every command directed at a device or tenant surface renders one of the fifteen defined command states, and no console view renders a command as applied on evidence weaker than a device acknowledgement.

The three-layer data-access model: administration and telemetry are metadata, counts, rates and statuses and never operational content; comparative cross-tenant analytics are anonymised aggregates enforced as an invariant; record-level operational content is reached only through one of the three named, audited, session-scoped classes. (enforcement: per-read enforcement on all console reads)

Ambient browsing of tenant content is Explicitly prohibited; exactly three named access classes exist — support session, compliance-emergency path, JBS access grant. (enforcement points cited: §8.1.2 three-layer model and §8.15)
The connectivity-loss protocol fires at 30, 60, and 120 minutes.
Degradation visible across more than one tenant is a platform incident owned in the Super Admin platform console; the tenant-facing panel keeps showing the honest per-tenant flag throughout.
Urgency never bypasses maker-checker or the critical class; no ambient access is opened during an incident. (applies to platform incidents)
Every agent activation record carries a reference to the deterministic trigger that preceded it; an activation with no antecedent trigger is rejected and raised as a platform incident.
No tenant sees another tenant's state, name, or data at any point. (applies to platform incidents)
Every incident record carries a classification, a named role owner, a detection source, a communication decision, and a verification checklist, and cannot be closed with any of them absent.

No metric, alert, or dashboard is accepted as audit evidence anywhere in the platform; every audit query resolves against the append-only tenant audit log. (binds MOD-SA-01 telemetry against MOD-SA-18)
Silence on the alerting path is itself detected and raised as an incident.

Any attempt to change one of the six enforced invariants fails for every account including the root, and the attempt is written to the platform audit log as an attempt on a locked setting.
None of the six enforced invariants has an off control, an approval path, or a configuration key on any screen, for any account including the root.

The six enforced invariants present no off control to any account, and a direct application programming interface attempt to disable one denies and is audited. (enforcement: Platform settings AND service layer — the refusal must be server-side, not interface-only)
All six invariants are unchangeable by the root; server-side refusal is independent of interface state. (enforcement: settings write endpoint)
All six invariants refuse every account including the root, through the interface and directly.
No enforced invariant can be disabled by any account. (enforcement: server-side refusal, no approval path)
No console role, including the root, can disable any of the six ENFORCED platform invariants.

Floor parity: no identity shape, tenant configuration, suspension state, or caller class permits an action that would breach a platform floor or one of the six enforced invariants. (enforcement: pre-release parity suite)
No deployment or migration may disable any of the six enforced invariants. (enforcement: deployment pipeline, all releases)
Six enforced invariants bind every account including the root, with no approval path around them; the eight-row platform floor register rejects rather than logs.
Pause and resume are each critical-class and separately approved. (enforcement: critical-class approval, root)
The emergency pause has no effect on on-device gates, specification checks, severity classification, or the Severity 1 hold.
Emergency pause never suppresses gates, specification checks, severity classification, or the Severity 1 hold; it renders as agent unavailability, never silence.
An approved emergency pause never alters specification gate behaviour, severity classification, containment launch, or the Severity 1 hold on any device.
The pause never suppresses the deterministic layer; it renders as unavailability, never silence; resume is a separate approved act; raised gates stay human-decidable throughout.
An emergency pause reduces agent activations to zero within the affected scope and leaves every deterministic on-device behaviour operating.
Resume is a separate action with its own approval and its own audit record; no automatic resume exists.
A per-tenant pause affects exactly one tenant and no other. (enforcement: cross-tenant isolation, an ENFORCED invariant)
Pause and resume are separate critical-class actions, each separately approved and audited.
No platform-level pause of the agentic layer ever suppresses the on-device deterministic layer. The deterministic backbone is not agent machinery and has no off switch.
An emergency pause parks in-flight agent runs at their next stage boundary, leaves raised gates human-decidable, and never suppresses the on-device deterministic layer.
The emergency pause renders as explicit agent unavailability and never suppresses the on-device deterministic layer.
A looser-than-floor value is rejected at entry with the bound stated and is never stored. The register rejects; it does not log. (enforcement: tenant-configuration registry, single enforcement point)
Tightening a bound surfaces non-conforming existing tenant values in a conformance report rather than rewriting them.
Changes to the floor register itself are critical class, meaning the root account approves them.
No tenant configuration can remove or weaken the Severity 1 floor, and an attempt is rejected at entry with the floor stated.

A locale pack with any untranslated key fails publication and names the keys.

A locale pack or content version with untranslated keys fails publication.
Change class is determined by the setting, never by the operator's role. (enforcement: automatic classification before submission)

A tenant override cannot defeat a global disable; tenants may be stricter, never looser than the platform floor, and the platform rejects rather than logs.
No password-only sign-in path exists for any console account. (settings category 23.7.5 Security and Access)

modules.purpose: Console capability section §8.18 / chapter-23 section 23.18. Stated purpose (L46125): maintain the append-only, immutable, complete platform audit log under the one-transaction guarantee, with cross-tenant mirroring and invariant-grade protections; §10.4 is cited alongside §8.18. Restated as: append-only platform audit log, read-only for every console role (L21095); Band B platform audit trail, mirrored to tenants where tenant-visible (L11675); platform audit log reader with class-filtered export for external retention (L76178); platform audit log used for access-model reconciliation and attestation (L57128, key_function FUNC-SA-RECONCILE-ACCESS); audit rows commit in the same transaction as the action (L98246). The one-transaction audit guarantee is itself one of the six ENFORCED invariants rendered locked by MOD-SA-07, so MOD-SA-18's core promise is enforced from another module's screen. Roles allowed: the broadest statement (L46125) is {Root Super Admin, Admin, Platform Engineer, Support, Tenant Admin (own mirrored stream), Read-only Auditor (own mirrored stream)}; narrower statements give {Root Super Admin, Admin} (L2442, L11675), all four console roles (L21095, L76178), and {Root Super Admin, Support, Read-only Auditor (mirrored)} (L60873). Declared features: FEAT-SA-18-01..04 (L46173, L46176, L46180, L46184) with nine FUNC-SA-18-* leaves (L46175–L46189); a second, incompatible numbering FEAT-SA-1801/1802/1803 with SUB-SA-1801/1802/1803 at L47834–L47836; and a third naming SUB-SA-AUDIT-EXPORT / SUB-SA-AUDIT-EDIT at L21095. No feature TITLES are carried in the extract for any of the three schemes. Ten acceptance criteria AC-SA-18-01..10 are all indexed at L46193 and ten test cases TEST-SA-18-* at L46195.

openQuestions: ATTRIBUTION METHOD, stated up front. Three methods were used and they are not equally strong. (a) EXACT — the entry carries module_id: this covers every control and screen I list without a bracket note, and it is the only exact method. (b) EXPLICIT KEY_FUNCTIONS — a module entry names the workflow ID in its key_functions array: MOD-SA-07 at L54620 names WF-FEAT-001/003/004 and WF-PLT-006/007; MOD-SA-01 at L55259 names WF-PLT-008/009; MOD-SA-18 at L57128 names only FUNC-SA-RECONCILE-ACCESS and no workflow at all. (c) LINE PROXIMITY — in CHK-013/CHK-014 the chapter-23 module anchor sits at the END of its section body, so a workflow belongs to the NEXT anchor at or after its line (L42925 -> MOD-SA-01 at L42979; L43996/L44469/L44500 -> MOD-SA-07 at L44633; L46094 -> MOD-SA-18 at L46125). In CHK-017 the convention is REVERSED — the anchor sits at the START of the block it labels — so the same rule misfires there and the nearest PRECEDING anchor is correct. Any tool that applies one rule to both chunks will misfile roughly forty workflows. Everything I label '[topical only]' has no module binding in the data at all.

MOD-SA-18 has effectively NO workflow inventory. Exactly one workflow in the entire 725-workflow extract binds to MOD-SA-18 by module_id or line proximity: 'An operator change and its audit event in one transaction' at L46094. The module's own CHK-017 entry (L57128) names one function and zero workflows. Everything else I list for it is topical inference. For a module whose acceptance criteria run to ten items (AC-SA-18-01..10, L46193) and whose guarantee is a platform invariant, that is a source gap, not a small module. Someone must author the audit-search, audit-export, mirroring and Platform Access History workflows before this ships.

MOD-SA-01 has exactly ONE control in the whole extract: the tenant/capability/incident filter at L47767, allowed to Platform Engineer only. Nothing else on the overview and health surface carries a module_id MOD-SA-01 control — no acknowledge, no open-incident, no drill-through, no incident close. The incident-close controls at L90758 and L107949 exist but carry no module binding, and the only two named onward actions from a metric tile (L107350) are bound to Tenant Metrics and Aggregates, not to this module. The overview's interaction model is essentially unspecified.

hardGates.statement: No user interface path exists, for any account including the root, to create an atom. Atoms arrive by backend migration. Enforcement point: Atom Registry — the absent create flow.
Enablement of an atom whose scenarios are pending or failing is refused at submit and again at apply, and both refusals are audit events. Enforcement point: eval gate.
No atom may be registered whose declared side-effects place a model in the deviation-triggering path; registration validation rejects it.
Disabling a detection-class atom has no effect on on-device severity classification or on the Severity 1 automatic hold. Enforcement point: on-device deterministic layer.
No user interface anywhere on the platform offers atom creation, and every atom in an environment traces to a migration reference.
No platform artifact, document, or interface text states or implies that an atom is built in under an hour (anti-overclaim rule).
The Agent Builder can compose only from the registry and offers no path to add to it. Enforcement point: Agent Builder interface and API.

No artificial-intelligence model participates in the evaluation of a specification, timing, sequence or evidence rule, and no code path exists by which a model output can set or alter a severity classification. Enforcement: registration validation, build-time static check.

A failing evaluation cannot be enabled by any account; if the scenarios themselves are wrong, changing the scenarios is itself a submitted change requiring approval, so the gate cannot be weakened by quietly editing its own test.
No agent, capability, or composed behaviour goes live without passing its evaluation scenarios. Hard enablement gate with no off position.
Server-side detection atoms are the mirror and confirmation path, never the trigger.
A tenant cannot reach another tenant's data by any route, and the control cannot be switched off by any account including the root — bears on the per-tenant enablement set on the atom record.

hardGates.statement: No tenant-composed agent becomes available on any floor without both the tenant's own approval chain and this module's review decision, and without passing sandbox evals. Enforcement: composed-agent review queue + sandbox.
Tenant-composed action agents cannot be submitted at V1; the Agent Builder offers reasoning composition only. Enforcement: Studio Agent Builder.
No agent can widen its own capability scope, alter its own memory grants, change its own type, or self-approve. Enforcement: agent record schema.
Disabling or pausing any agent leaves on-device severity classification and the Severity 1 automatic hold unchanged.
Every agent activation record carries a reference to the deterministic trigger that preceded it; an activation with no antecedent trigger is rejected and raised as a platform incident.

Every agent effect on state or on a worker is traceable either to a named pre-authorised policy object approved through the Studio approval chain, or to a named human gate decision in the Client Command Center.
When released, the Vision Reasoning Agent's registration declares no side-effect in the deviation-triggering path and no severity write.
When released, the agent's type determines its governance; a state-changing effect re-types it to action and it inherits action-agent governance. Enforcement: agent record definition validation.
Agents are records, not code. One agent-record schema exists; every agent, platform-authored or tenant-composed, is an instance of it with nine fields.

The governance-binding field's declared values are `authoring-time policy`, `runtime human gate`, and `none — reasoning agent`; the Prevention Agent carries the first, the Deviation and Containment Agent the second for proposals beyond pre-authorised containment, and the Shift Handoff Agent and every tenant-composed agent the third.
An agent definition whose runs are on the record cannot be deleted; its history must remain explicable.

The evaluation gate sits after approval rather than before it, so an approved change that fails a scenario still does not ship and the prior version stays in force. Applies to prompt, model config and provider config changes.
There is no path by which an agent acquires a tool at runtime that its record does not name. Enforcement: capability scope on the agent record.
A residency-affecting provider change is a critical-class change requiring root approval.
Model, provider and tool failover never broadens an agent's capability scope, memory grants, tenant scope, or governance binding. Enforcement: permissions re-read from the agent record.
The semantic cache is keyed within a single tenant and by content version; no cache entry is reachable across tenants.
Emergency pause never suppresses gates, specification checks, severity classification, or the Severity 1 hold; it renders as agent unavailability, never silence.
No agent, capability, or composed behaviour goes live without passing its evaluation scenarios (the hard enablement gate with no off position).

Specification gates are hard and always; the evaluation gate is hard and always including for the root account; the qualification gate is the only configurable gate, with strict blocking as its default.

hardGates.statement: No mechanism exists by which one tenant's memory becomes readable by another tenant or is used as external training data. Enforcement: architectural isolation, not a permission setting.
Profile memory holds aggregates only; no individual-level profile record can be created. Enforcement: profile memory store contract.
No Lane-B proposal is applied without a recorded decision by a Quality Manager or above in the tenant's own Client Command Center. Enforcement: Lane-B publication pipeline.
An undecided Lane-B proposal receives a 30-day stale flag and never expires or is discarded silently. Enforcement: proposal aging scheduler.
In-flight runs remain pinned to the workflow version they started on through any Lane-B publication. Enforcement: version pinning.
Memory has no export path on any surface at the first version, and this blueprint proposes none. Enforcement point: export controls; applies to class six memory.
No agent holds a write grant to procedural memory; procedural content changes only through Studio publication. Enforcement: grant model.
Profile memory contains aggregates only; a write carrying identifiable per-worker content is rejected. Enforcement: profile memory write path.
No query path exists that can return another tenant's memory, including under failover, cache, index, or support-session conditions. Enforcement: query layer, cache keying, index partitioning.
Nothing from any store is used as external training data, and no fine-tuning of any model occurs. Enforcement: model lifecycle and data-export paths.
A tenant retention value outside the platform bounds is rejected at entry with the bound stated, never accepted and logged. Enforcement: retention register.
Cross-tenant sharing of learned material is Explicitly prohibited; strict tenant isolation with no external training data. Enforcement point recorded literally as `MOD-STU-16`, `MOD-SA-04`, `§8.4.2`.
Worker-level data is held as purpose-bound aggregates, not raw behavioural feeds. Enforcement: profile memory store with personal-information-redaction policy.
A tenant cannot reach another tenant's data by any route, and the control cannot be switched off by any account including the root.
Availability is sacrificed to isolation without hesitation, in that order. Isolation is never traded for availability. Enforcement: fallback safety priority order.
A tenant retention value looser than the floor is rejected at the point of entry with the bound stated, rather than accepted and logged.
Retention-value changes, for the horizon or a bound, for any tenant, are critical class requiring root approval.

Only approved content enters the corpus; the agent selects only from what the quality team sanctioned; embeddings change how an asset is found, never whether it was approved. Enforcement: corpus curation gate.
Agents propose and never apply a Lane B change. Enforcement: two-lane learning loop.
Configured values are a floor, not a ceiling: the engineer's value is the starting point the platform reasons from, and the loop refines around it only through the Lane B gate.

Anonymisation is the platform's one irreversible act: worker personal data anonymises at 24 months for standard tenants; measurement, result and evidence survive; identity becomes a pseudonym; it never happens in Regulated-Industry mode.
Switching a tenant into Regulated mode later does not resurrect anonymised identities — an onboarding conversation, not a surprise.
The legal-hold check precedes erasure execution, always. Legal hold outranks erasure; a preservation obligation defeats an erasure request and the requester is told so.
Under the no-purge lifecycle model storage accumulates perpetually; the tiering curve is the cost lever; there is no delete lever at all.
The console offers no ambient browsing of tenant content; every record-level access opens a named, reason-required, audited session mirrored to the tenant.
