openQuestions: BUILD-BLOCKING — MOD-SA-04 has ZERO actionable controls. Not one row in the 759-entry raw controls[] extraction, nor in the 608-entry deduplicated inventory (registries/generated/actionable-controls.json), carries module_id=MOD-SA-04. A line-window sweep around both of its screens (SCR-SA-MEMORY L87029, SCR-SA-FOOTPRINT L87611) and around its whole CHK-013 card (L43467-43632) returns nothing. Yet the module owns 4 features (FEAT-SA-04-01..04 at L43581/43588/43592/43599) and 16 functions (L43583-43605). Concretely undefined: how a per-type retention default is set, how a redaction policy is edited, how a re-index is triggered, and what the cross-tenant footprint view actually shows. The only adjacent affordance is Admin 'Trigger a coaching-corpus re-index', which appears solely as role-permission text at L42713 and never as a control with a screen, an approval class, or an effect. MOD-SA-02 has 4 controls by module_id and MOD-SA-03 has 2, so this is not a uniform extraction failure.

ACCEPTANCE-CRITERION COVERAGE IS PARTIAL. registries/raw/identifier-index.json shows AC-SA-02-01..10 at L43253-43262, AC-SA-03-01..09 at L43433-43441, and AC-SA-04-01..10 at L43623-43632 — 29 criteria. Only 13 were extracted into business_rules at all, and every one of those 13 has is_hard_gate=true. Missing entirely: AC-SA-02-02, -04, -05, -08, -09, -10; AC-SA-03-01, -02, -03, -05, -07; AC-SA-04-01, -02, -04, -06, -09. Their gate status, statements and enforcement points are unknown from this data. Do not assume they are soft: the extracted subset is 13-for-13 hard. Also note AC-SA-03 stops at -09 while both 02 and 04 run to -10, so MOD-SA-03 has one fewer criterion by design or by omission — the source does not say which.

SCREEN IDENTIFIER COLLISION between CHK-013 and CHK-015, off by one module. In CHK-013, SCR-SA-02=Atom registry list and atom detail (L42794), SCR-SA-03=Agent roster and agent detail (L42795), SCR-SA-04=Composed-agent review queue (L42796), SCR-SA-05=Memory administration and cross-tenant footprint (L42797). In CHK-015, SCR-SA-03=Atom Registry / 'MOD-SA-02 all features' (L48732), SCR-SA-04=Agents and composed-agent review / 'MOD-SA-03 all features' (L48733), SCR-SA-05=Memory administration / 'MOD-SA-04 all features' (L48734). SCR-SA-03 therefore names two different screens and SCR-SA-05 is the only number where the two chunks agree. Any build that keys off SCR-SA-NN will wire the atom registry to the agent roster. Pick one numbering and record which chunk lost.

DEC-FEAT-001 is open and blocks MOD-SA-02's core action. §8.2.2 makes atom enablement a Platform Engineer change requiring Admin approval; §8.19 makes platform-side tenant current-value changes, including feature enablement, Admin actions. Both readings are explicitly preserved, never resolved (L43209, L15893, L21098, L65434, L67891, L108057, L111473, L113836, L118441; recorded as a contradiction at L4638, L9426, L46211, L54664). The best the corpus offers is a recommendation, not a decision: 'split by kind — capability-level controls follow the Engineer-to-Admin path; commercial entitlement controls are Admin actions' (L46668). Until decided, the 'Submit tenant enablement change' control at L43158 has no settled maker.

DEC-AGENTLC-001 is open and blocks MOD-SA-03 after approval. The composition-review-approval path is stated; deprecation, disablement, rollback of a DEPLOYED composed agent, and the fate of its in-flight runs are not (L43312, L33994, L55336, L88617, L106902, L110655). L34736 puts it plainly: a misbehaving composed reasoning agent has no stated off switch short of the platform-wide emergency pause. Two incompatible interim positions are on record: L21543 says 'until decided, no console role holds this authority and the build denies it, naming the decision'; L117766 says 'assume DEC-AGENTLC-001 reuses emergency-pause semantics'; L72685 says validation refuses a disablement request that cannot state what happens to in-flight work. L43312 marks it must-resolve-before-the-Agent-Builder-ships. Pick one before writing the disable path.

WHO DECIDES A COMPOSED-AGENT REVIEW has three readings. The control at L43339 allows ROLE-PLAT-ROOT, ROLE-PLAT-ADMIN and ROLE-PLAT-ENG. The Admin role card lists 'Decide a composed-agent submission' under may (L42713). The Platform Engineer role card ALSO lists it under may, as 'technical review under the §8.8 discipline' (L42714) — while the same entry's may_not forbids the Platform Engineer to 'Author or edit an agent definition'. And the MOD-SA-03 module record at L98231 narrows roles_allowed to {Admin} alone. Whether the Platform Engineer decides, technically reviews, or merely proposes is unsettled.

MODULE roles_allowed CONTRADICT ACROSS CHUNKS for all three modules, and one is empty. MOD-SA-02: {Platform Engineer, Admin} at L2442 and L98230; {Root Super Admin, Platform Engineer} at L11659; all four console roles at L21079 and L43166; {Platform Engineer} alone at L47786, L60857, L67903; EMPTY at L116399. MOD-SA-03: all four at L21080 and L43347; {Platform Engineer} at L47789; {Platform Engineer, platform Admin} at L55295; {Platform Engineer, Root Super Admin} at L60858; {Admin} ALONE at L98231; EMPTY at L116399. MOD-SA-04: all four at L21081 and L43536; {Platform Engineer} at L47792 and L60859; EMPTY ARRAY at L98232 and L116399. The four-role cut (L43166/43347/43536) is the most detailed and uses the ROLE-PLAT-* identifiers, so treat it as primary — but say so explicitly rather than letting an implementer pick the narrow cut.

OWNERSHIP CONFLICT — right-to-erasure and retention sit in two modules at once. The L86041 cut of MOD-SA-04 lists 'right-to-erasure workflow' and 'retention defaults' among its key functions, and L21081 states the module is 'Memory store configuration and per-type retention'. But every erasure and legal-hold CONTROL carries module_id MOD-SA-17: the five-step guided erasure sequence (L45997), the erasure requests list (L97663), the no-undo/no-de-anonymise absence control (L97560), the legal hold (L117354). The erasure workflow itself sits at L97649 in the §8.17 neighbourhood. Decide whether MOD-SA-04 administers policy while MOD-SA-17 executes requests, or whether L86041 is simply wrong — the current data would have two teams build the same screen.

PER-TYPE RETENTION VALUES ARE NEVER STATED, though per-type retention is the module's headline job (L2442, L21081, L86041, L98232). Every retention number in the corpus is either global or belongs elsewhere: the 15-year hot-retrievability horizon (L4718, L7537, L45950, L74782), 24-month profile-memory anonymisation (L43558, L86992), 24-month orchestrator trace retention which belongs to MOD-SA-06 (L43837, L47800). No default, bound, or floor is given for the working, episodic, semantic or procedural store individually. The working store's only stated bound is behavioural — 'discarded at run scope' (L9505).

LANE-B SURFACE INCONSISTENCY. MOD-SA-04 owns OBJ-SA-LANEB, the publication pipeline record (L43547), and the workflow at L43485 correctly lists SURF-SA among its surfaces. But 'Lane B from signal to floor' at L87691 lists only SURF-CC, SURF-STU, SURF-DOH and SURF-FL — no SURF-SA — so it falls out of any surfaces_touched filter despite describing the pipeline this module administers. One of the two entries is wrong about where the pipeline lives.

DEC-LANEB-001 is open and bears directly on MOD-SA-04's pipeline: §5.11.1 requires explicit human sign-off at Author, Reviewer and Release Authority before any workflow content reaches the frontline, while §5.16.3 and §6.7.4 have an approved Lane-B proposal auto-publish a patch with 'no second approval, no ceremony' (L43483, L87683, and 30+ further restatements including L3816, L7233, L11294, L91021, L106958 which notes neither reading is adopted). Two further unresolved riders: DEC-PKGFIELD-001 — the authoritative field-by-field assignment of package-borne versus server-only values, said to live in the Part VII package contract, which does not enumerate it (L43483, L87683) — so the package test cannot be applied deterministically; and L43530, which notes a Lane-B patch would be v2.1.1 under semantic versioning whereas the canonical illustrative republish of the same workflow is v2.2.0, a minor version requiring the Job Owner's adoption decision.

EMERGENCY PAUSE IS UNPARENTED. It stops agent activity — the objects MOD-SA-03 administers — yet not one of its many controls carries module_id MOD-SA-03. They appear under SCR-SA-PAUSE (L70933), the literal string 'Emergency pause control' (L65613-65614), 'Super Admin module 5 (eval harness gate view panel 4)' (L113588), MOD-SA-07 (L54979), and 'unstated' (L87828, L87854, L104586). Initiation authority is explicitly open: L87854 says 'initiation authority open under DEC-PAUSE-001', L91289 records site-scoped pause as R&D under DEC-AIPAUSE-001, and L84064 has platform Admin OR Platform Engineer initiating while root approves. Decide which module owns the pause screen before two teams build it.

NOTIFICATION IDENTIFIERS EXIST WITH NO CONTENT. NOTIF-SA-02-01..05 (L43241-43245), NOTIF-SA-03-01..05 (L43421-43425) and NOTIF-SA-04-01..05 (L43611-43615) appear in both the identifier index and registries/generated/notifications.json, each carrying only an id, a source line and status 'not-represented'. No trigger, recipient, channel, or state progression is recorded for any of the fifteen. By contrast, notification state progressions ARE spelled out elsewhere in the corpus (for example NOTIF-SA-08-04 at L44863). Fifteen notifications will be built from nothing unless these are re-extracted from the source lines.

FEATURE AND FUNCTION TITLES ARE ABSENT EVERYWHERE. All 22 FEAT-SA-02/03/04 rows and all 55 FUNC-SA-02/03/04 rows in registries/generated/features.json and functions.json carry id, sourceLine and surface only — no label. The module records give the id lists (L43166, L43347, L43536) but never say what any feature does. The implementation team can locate each in the source but cannot learn its scope from these registries. Note also a parallel, incompatible identifier scheme in CHK-014: FEAT-SA-0201/0202/0203 at L47786-47788, FEAT-SA-0301..0303 at L47789-47791, FEAT-SA-0401..0403 at L47792-47794 — three features per module rather than four or five. Which scheme is canonical is not stated.

BUSINESS USE CASES EXIST FOR TWO OF THE THREE MODULES. UC-SA-020..023 (four, all at L15968) and UC-SA-030..032 (three, all at L16112) are indexed; there is no UC-SA-04x anywhere in registries/raw/identifier-index.json. Whether MOD-SA-04 genuinely has no use cases or whether they were never written is not recoverable from this data — and given that the module also has zero controls, the two gaps probably share a cause.

MALFORMED STATE ENUMERATION — the coaching-corpus index vocabulary at L43548 reads ['current','re-indexing','current','stale'], listing 'current' twice. The clean three-state cut of the same concept is at L8711: ['indexing','current','stale pending re-index']. A third variant at L96284 uses ['Indexed','Queued for indexing','Indexing unavailable — retrieval is using the previous index']. Three vocabularies for one index; none is marked authoritative.

SEMANTIC MEMORY WRITE PRECEDENCE IS UNRESOLVED AND HAS NO GOVERNING DECISION. L9555 records that the source states curated ingestion PLUS agents write the semantic store without stating precedence, and notes 'curation-wins is the only reading consistent with the platform never invents content' — but governing_decision is null, so no DEC identifier tracks it. OBJ-074's states ['ingested','curated','retained'] (L9543) do not settle write ordering either.

OBJECTS WITH EMPTY STATE ARRAYS, where a lifecycle is plainly implied. OBJ-SA-ENABLEMENT, the per-tenant enablement entry (L43177) — yet the atom record's own vocabulary distinguishes 'enabled platform-wide' from 'enabled per tenant' (L43178), so per-tenant enablement clearly has states. OBJ-SA-REDACT, the redaction policy (L43547) — MOD-SA-04's key function 'personal-data-redaction policy' (L98232) needs a lifecycle to be approvable. OBJ-AGENT-RECORD (L113201). Each needs its states named before a state machine can be written.

MOD-SA-02's REGISTRATION-REFUSAL PATH HAS NO SURFACE. AC-SA-02-06 (L43258) requires registration validation to reject any atom whose declared side-effects place a model in the deviation-triggering path, and L86848 gives 'rejected at registration' as a terminal state of the atom workflow. But since no create-atom control exists for any account (AC-SA-02-01 at L43253, AC-AI-007-1 at L86948) and atoms arrive by backend migration, nothing in the extraction says where a rejected registration is shown, to whom, or whether it is audited. The registry list filters (L43158) filter on domain grouping, status, eval verdict and detection class — no 'rejected' facet is named.

MODEL AND INFERENCE IS ASSIGNED TO MOD-SA-03 BY SCREEN ONLY. SCR-SA-MODELS carries module_id=MOD-SA-03 (L87143), pulling model routing, prompts, provider bindings, the semantic cache and quotas into this module — yet MOD-SA-03's stated purpose at L43347 is confined to agent records and composed-agent review and never mentions any of it. Four decisions in that block are open: DEC-MODEL-001 model and provider selection (L87091), DEC-PROMPT-001 prompt authorship, versioning, approval class and trace visibility (L87097), DEC-CACHE-001 semantic cache scope and invalidation (L87165), DEC-QUOTA-001 per-tenant token ceiling and concurrency (L87566). DEC-CONF-001 leaves OBJ-AI-CONFPOL with no states at all (L88402). Also note L87089: Gemini Embedding 2.0 is the ONLY model or provider named anywhere in the source, and it is named for the coaching-corpus index, not for any agent router role.

THE CROSS-TENANT FOOTPRINT VIEW IS CONSTRAINED TO NOTHING VISIBLE. SCR-SA-FOOTPRINT exists (L87611) and MOD-SA-04 owns it, but memory content is 'Unavailable — counts and volume only' for Root Super Admin (L97152), platform Admin (L97153) and Platform Engineer (L97154), and flatly 'Unavailable' for Support (L97155) and JBS delivery staff (L97156); Tenant Admin may not view it at all (L87047); there is no export path at V1 (L96871) and no tenant-facing memory content surface (L97147). Which counts and which volume dimensions the screen renders is nowhere stated. Design it from the four named storage-metering dimensions at L96973 (evidence media, workflow packages, the parts registry, training content) only if the client confirms that mapping — the source does not make it.

hardGates.statement: No write capability exists inside a normal support session for any account including the root — read-only without exception.
A session cannot open without a ticket-linked reason class.
Sessions expire at their time box, default two hours, and cannot be extended in place.
A persistent banner naming the engineer and start time renders to the tenant for the whole session, with a working End-session control.
Pressing End session terminates platform access immediately.
The compliance-emergency path requires a named emergency class and two authorisations and cannot be initiated by one person.
The emergency session's scope is declared before it opens and cannot be widened during it.
The compliance-emergency path is the only write path into tenant data and the only entry into a compliance-suspended tenant.
No ambient browsing capability exists anywhere on the console.
Ambient browsing of tenant content is Explicitly prohibited; exactly three named access classes exist — support session, compliance-emergency path, JBS access grant.

No tenant record is read while the tenant cannot see that it is being read; if the banner cannot render, the session is suspended and no further reads are served until the banner is confirmed visible.
No banner means no session: the session does not open, or terminates, if the banner cannot be shown — visibility is a precondition of the access rather than a decoration on it.
Banner text is fixed in the source: 'Platform support is viewing your workspace. Started [time]. Engineer [name]. End session.'
No write operation of any kind is reachable inside a normal support session; a support-tool credential cannot be used outside an open session and dies at session end.
An automatic post-session report is generated for the tenant on every close, including a close by time-box expiry.
The tenant automatically receives a post-session report after a compliance-emergency session; the control to suppress the tenant report does not exist.
No End-session control is offered for the compliance-emergency class, because an emergency access the tenant could terminate would not be an emergency access.
Access outside the declared emergency scope is refused and recorded, not merely logged as a warning; widening requires a new request with new authorisations, never an in-session widening.
Legal-hold release and compliance-emergency-path opening each require two distinct approving identities.
The compliance-emergency path requires two authorisations, the root and one Admin, and this cannot be reduced to one.
Authorisations are re-evaluated at session open, not only at authorisation time; a revoked authorisation can never open a compliance-emergency session.

No write capability exists in a support session; the banner is present for the entire session with a working End-session control; sessions expire at the configured time box, default two hours; every action mirrors to the tenant's audit stream.

Two authorisations are required and one of them is the root; scope is declared before the session opens; an automatic post-session report reaches the tenant; this is the only path with write capability into tenant data.
Tenant termination of a support session is immediate and unconditional; a failed termination is recorded, not hidden.
No in-place extension of a support session; overruns are recorded.
One tenant per session; no in-place extension; actions never exceed the declared scope.
Session scope is fixed at open and is not recomputed from role; no open session gains write capability.
Session history is never deleted; no session survives disablement. Anonymisation applies to worker personal data and not to platform access records.
The only platform-side entry into a compliance-suspended tenant is the dual-authorised compliance-emergency path.
No tenant role can authenticate to the Super Admin platform console under any configuration, including during a support session, a compliance-emergency session, or a JBS grant.
No evidence record can be mutated or deleted on any surface, including through the compliance-emergency path, which writes rather than erases.
No console action is qualification-gated, and no console role can write a tenant qualification outside the compliance-emergency path.
Removing the last Tenant Admin is refused, with the rule named, and no override exists on any surface — including inside a support session.
A compliance-emergency session requires two distinct authorising identities: the root plus one Admin. Neither alone opens the session.
Exactly three access classes exist and no path reaches tenant content outside them; no ambient browsing exists anywhere on the console.
No ambient browsing exists anywhere on the console. Layer 3 record-level content is reached only through an audited, session-scoped access under one of the three named access classes.
Under STATE-06 the cause is always named — tenant hard suspension, an archived object, a role without write authority, or a support session; 'read-only' alone is never shown.

openQuestions: SCREEN NUMBERING IS SELF-CONTRADICTORY ACROSS THE SOURCE. Two incompatible SCR-SA-* numbering schemes exist for exactly these five modules. Scheme A (L42811-L42816, restated L45498-L45997): SCR-SA-19 Fleet/device detail, SCR-SA-20 Broadcast composer, SCR-SA-21 Support sessions, SCR-SA-22 Compliance-emergency, SCR-SA-23 JBS grants, SCR-SA-24 Data lifecycle. Scheme B (L48745-L48749): SCR-SA-16 Devices and fleet, SCR-SA-17 Platform notifications, SCR-SA-18 Support access sessions, SCR-SA-19 JBS access grants, SCR-SA-20 Data lifecycle and archival. SCR-SA-19 and SCR-SA-20 therefore name two different screens each. No governing decision identifier is attached to this conflict in the extract. An implementation team cannot key routes off SCR-SA numbers until this is resolved.

DEC-WIPE-001 IS UNRESOLVED AND IT BLOCKS MOD-SA-13's CENTRAL RULE. Sync-then-wipe requires a final sync attempt before erasure (L4624, L45570 AC-SA-13-04, L103888 AC-SEC-501), which an offline device cannot perform. The source states neither how long a wipe may remain pending nor what happens if the device never returns (raised at L7504, L10623, L49745, L53041, L60277, L71331, L78348, L81026, L94810, L98375, L100878, L103781, L107425, L111165, L113402, L117758 — 15+ restatements, all open). Two readings are preserved: 'final sync is a precondition, so a device that never reconnects is never wiped' vs 'wipe anyway, recording what was lost' (L103781, L113409). L113409 notes Option A destroys unsynced evidence and is saved only by the word 'silently'. The extract records at L81026 that automatic device wipe on prolonged offline was PERMANENTLY REJECTED at V1 (P16, reconciliation closed_action_sets), which constrains but does not decide the question.

DEVICE OWNERSHIP IS SPLIT IN THE SOURCE ITSELF (DEC-ENROLL-001 / DEC-DEVOWN-001, both open). §7.5.2 assigns device enrolment and lifecycle to the Super Admin console; §8.13.4 makes enrolment tenant self-service with the console keeping policy, telemetry and wipe authority (L8459, L10324, L67731, L71656, L75992). AC-SA-13-02 at L45570 is a hard gate stating no console role can enroll a tenant's device. Build against AC-SA-13-02, but the object-authority split is unresolved and MOD-SA-13's object cards contradict each other on owner (OBJ-033 owner SURF-SA at L8456 vs OBJ-034 Device enrollment owner SURF-DOH at L8475 vs 'SURF-SA (policy) / tenant (fleet ownership)' at L45517).

DEVICE WIPE IS NOT ONE OF THE FIVE COMMAND CLASSES AND NO MECHANISM IS NAMED (DEC-CMDCLASS-001, open, raised new at L51494/L51551). §7.2.2 closes the command channel at five classes (lot release, reassignment or substitution, qualification clearance, suspension, version change) yet §7.11 and §8.13.3 require a remote wipe instruction to reach a device. CMD-SUSP-005 device wipe is listed in the suspension-class panel while simultaneously marked 'reaches the device but is not one of the five named classes' (L51494). L51334 records fifteen command instances sitting cleanly inside a named class and one (device wipe) that does not. The transport for the single most consequential MOD-SA-13 command is undefined.

JBS GRANT WRITE CAPABILITY IS GENUINELY AMBIGUOUS (DEC-JBSWRITE-001, open). §8.16 places JBS access under 'exactly the same discipline' as the other classes while §8.15.2 says the compliance-emergency path is 'the only one with write capability'; §8.8.5 nevertheless contemplates JBS authoring capacity that writes (L14877, L14878, L17363, L23833, L74630). The extract's recommendation at L14877 is read-only always, to keep §8.15.2 literally true — but it is a recommendation, not an adopted position. MOD-SA-16 cannot be built until this is decided.

MOD-SA-16 HAS ALMOST NO EXTRACTED SURFACE DETAIL. Exactly ONE actionable control is extracted for the whole module (the revocation control at L45871). No control is extracted for drafting a grant, submitting it, approving it, or scoping it, despite AC-SA-16-02 (L45938) making scope, time box and reason mandatory before submission and despite FUNC-SA-16-01-A1..A3, 16-02-A1..A2, 16-03-A1..A2 (L45924-L45934) existing as function identifiers. Similarly only ONE control (wipe) plus its variants is extracted for MOD-SA-13, none for setting the minimum device specification, the release channel, the application-version floor or the cache-validity rule, all of which the module is stated to own (L45517, L76078). Treat the control lists above as a floor, not a census.

THE AC-SA-1x ACCEPTANCE-CRITERION SEQUENCES HAVE GAPS. Extracted: AC-SA-13-02..06 (no -01); AC-SA-14-01..04, 06, 07 (no -05); AC-SA-15-01..05, 07, 08, 10, 11 (no -06, -09); AC-SA-16-01, -02, -06 (no -03, -04, -05); AC-SA-17-01, -02, -04..09, -11 (no -03, -10). Roughly a dozen numbered acceptance criteria that the source's own numbering implies exist are absent from the extract. Do not read the hard-gate lists above as the complete criterion set for any of these five modules.

LEGAL HOLD DUAL-APPROVAL SCOPE CONFLICTS (no governing decision recorded). §10.1 specifies dual approval on RELEASE only; §8.17.3 specifies dual approval on BOTH place and release; §8.8.3 places both in the critical class (L97410). AC-SA-17-04 at L46074 adopts the both-ends reading. Implementers must know which one is contractual.

LEGAL HOLD vs ANONYMISATION IS UNDECIDED (DEC-SEC-019, New — Client Decision Required, L104368). The source states a hold suspends tiering and compliance-driven deletion but says nothing about anonymisation — which is the one irreversible act and exactly the attribution a hold exists to preserve (L97408, L104368). AC-SCHED-345 at L102158 requires the hold check per object on BOTH the tiering and anonymisation handlers, which implies suspension, but that is an inference from a test, not a stated rule.

DEC-ANON-001 IS 'PRESUMED YES', NOT CONFIRMED (L2039, L10641, L19051, L44187, L97583, L114141, L117767). The 24-month anonymisation horizon sits directly against the no-purge model: nothing ceases to exist, yet anonymisation permanently and irreversibly destroys a category of information (L97583). The whole of MOD-SA-17's anonymisation area rests on an unconfirmed drafting presumption.

DEC-DELETE-001 IS THE NO-PURGE MODEL'S SINGLE DEPENDENCY AND IT IS CLIENT-OWED AND OPEN (L1917, L10617, L97369, L100043, L104345, L113 area, L117769). Deletion occurs only where a named compliance standard requires it, and the list of standards has not landed. L1917 states the working position: until the list lands, no deletion path is built or promised. The erasure workflow's execution stage therefore has no defined trigger set.

AUDIT IMMUTABILITY vs ERASURE IS UNRECONCILED (L97689). The audit log is append-only with no delete or edit path on any surface, yet the erasure workflow writes a certificate wherever deletion actually occurs and a genuine erasure obligation reaches audit rows. Separately at L74786 the source reconciles anonymisation with append-only audit only by asserting it operates on the identity-resolution layer rather than rewriting rows — that reconciliation is stated as a necessary inference, not as a source fact.

SUPPORT-SESSION RE-OPEN BEHAVIOUR IS UNSPECIFIED AND THE DECISION IDENTIFIER COLLIDES. After a tenant terminates a session from the banner, may the same engineer immediately re-open on the same ticket? Does a cool-down apply? Does a re-open notify the Tenant Admin? Raised as DEC-SUPPORT-001 at L61211 and again at L64642; DEC-SUP-001 at L107877 covers consequences of repeated tenant-initiated termination plus support RTO (blueprint recommends failing closed). SEPARATELY, the identifier DEC-SUPPORT-001 is reused for three unrelated questions: session re-open (L61211, L64642), whether support impersonation exists at all (L112707), and how the JBS access class may be restricted per tenant (L115680). DEC-SUPPORT-002 at L112726 asks whether tenant consent is required before a session opens or only visible after. The identifier namespace itself is unsafe here.

DEC-IMPERSONATE-001 IS UNRESOLVED AND TOUCHES MOD-SA-15 DIRECTLY (L17647, L20175). §4.12.3 lists 'cross-tenant visibility and impersonation control' among Super Admin functions while Part VIII defines no impersonation feature, states support sessions are read-only without exception, closes access classes at three, and forbids an acting-as-role record. Build nothing for impersonation until this closes.

THE TENANT BANNER AND End-session CONTROL ARE ATTACHED ONLY TO THE NORMAL SUPPORT SESSION (L14878). §8.15.1 says nothing about whether the compliance-emergency path or the JBS grant carry a banner. L64810 resolves it one way for the emergency class — no End-session control exists, because an emergency access the tenant could terminate would not be an emergency access — but leaves the JBS grant unaddressed.

THE CRITICAL-CLASS SET IS DESCRIBED AS TEN AND ENUMERATED AS ELEVEN (L15360, L55942, L65359). The enumeration names tier publication, compliance suspension, all-tenant broadcast, device wipe and de-authorisation, emergency pause, emergency resume, erasure and archival execution, retention-value changes, legal-hold place and release, severity-catalog changes, floor-register changes. Four of these eleven belong to the modules mapped here. Separately, L113859 records that an all-tenant broadcast is critical class while a global capability disable — which reaches every tenant with far greater operational effect — is not on the list at all.

THE ROOT IS THE ONLY CRITICAL APPROVER AND ROOT UNAVAILABILITY FREEZES FOUR OF THESE FIVE MODULES (DEC-ROOTSUCC-001 / DEC-ROOTSOD-001, unresolved, L55989). Approving one's own critical action is permitted for the root because the source assigns no second critical approver — directly against the platform's own self-approval prohibition, recorded as an Assumption. Root unavailability freezes device wipe (MOD-SA-13), all-tenant broadcast (MOD-SA-14), compliance-emergency authorisation (MOD-SA-15), JBS grant issue (MOD-SA-16), and retention changes, legal hold, archival and erasure (MOD-SA-17). FB-EMERG-001 at L64856 names the fallback when the root is unreachable during an incident: the remaining access classes only — there is no substitute authoriser.

DEC-SYNC-001 IS AN ADOPTED WORKING POSITION, NOT SoW FACT, AND ITS RATIFICATION IS OUTSTANDING (25 instances, first at L1678). Adopted 2026-08-14, Option C: at reconnection, phase 1 stop-class commands (suspension in all three states, device de-authorisation, remote wipe, tenant compliance stop) apply FIRST, then the full capture upload, then enabling-class commands. This directly orders MOD-SA-13's wipe delivery against the sync-then-wipe protection, and L80072 records that §8.13.1's cache-validity rule argues commands-first while §7.11 and §8.13.3's sync-then-wipe rule argues captures-first, with one source sentence supporting each and neither subordinate.

DEC-STORE-001 (device storage-full behaviour) FAILS THE ORPHAN-GATE CHECK AS A SOURCE GAP. FB-DEVICE-STORAGE has no defined behaviour and no owner, so the device storage-full terminal state is undefined (reconciliation residual_contradictions). Storage-pressure signals are nonetheless a named element of the MOD-SA-13 fleet screen at L53070, so the console must render a signal whose downstream behaviour does not exist.

MOD-SA-14's OBJECT BOUNDARY IS SPLIT AND SHOULD BE READ CAREFULLY. OBJ-SA-BROADCAST and OBJ-SA-AUDIENCESNAPSHOT are SURF-SA-owned (L45633), but the Notification object every broadcast rides on is owned by SURF-DOH (L9203, L2273, L61127) with its own nineteen-state vocabulary. AC-SA-15-04 at L45832 further notes the tenant banner's enforcement point is 'Tenant UI rendering property (not the notification machinery)'. The console composes and snapshots; it does not own delivery state.

MOD-SA-13's connectivity and health workflows are attributed by DOMAIN-NAME, not by module_id or line proximity. The connectivity-loss protocol (L36004), site-wide connectivity loss thresholds (L102004) and the health-verdict workflow (L107393) touch SURF-SA and feed the fleet telemetry the §8.13 screen renders (L53070), but the source never states which module owns the 30/60/120-minute protocol. Confirm ownership before assigning them to a MOD-SA-13 build lane.

IDENTIFIER-INDEX COUNTS ARE NOT MODULE-CONTENT COUNTS. registries/raw/identifier-index.json records exactly three source lines for each of MOD-SA-13 (4624, 11670, 21090), MOD-SA-14 (4625, 11671, 21091), MOD-SA-15 (4626, 11672, 21092), MOD-SA-16 (4627, 11673, 21093) and MOD-SA-17 (4628, 4800, 4801) — those are literal identifier-token occurrences, not the modules' footprint. The extract carries module declarations for these five at many further lines (L21090, L42747, L45502, L53070, L54495, L54998, L55070, L60868, L75346, L76078, L98241, L99430, L116399) where the identifier string itself does not appear. The canonical per-surface figure is 19 SA capability sections (§8.1–§8.20); no per-module screen or control count is published anywhere.

value.topic: SURF-SA cross-cutting access spine: the three named platform access classes (support session, compliance-emergency path, JBS access grant), the "no ambient browsing" closure, and the eight per-surface access classes

findings.claim: CLASS 1 — NORMAL SUPPORT SESSION, who may open it. Primary operator is Support (ROLE-PLAT-SUP). Support 'may open a time-boxed read-only session into one tenant against a ticket-linked reason class'.

Support session — module roles_allowed is INCONSISTENT across passages: {Support} only (L2442); {Root, Admin, Support} (L11672, L21092, L60870, L76178, L98243); {Root, Admin, Platform Engineer, Support} (L45757, L116399); {ROLE-PLAT-ROOT/ADMIN/ENG/SUP} (L42749); {Support, Admin} (L99430). Implementers must treat the opener set as unsettled, not derive it from one row.

Support session preconditions (hard gates): a session cannot open without a ticket-linked reason class (AC-SA-15-02); the reason-class selector must be chosen BEFORE the tenant selector enables, explicitly 'preventing browse-first-justify-later'; the open form takes reason class from a closed list, a mandatory ticket reference, scope, and the two-hour default box.

Support session capability: READ-ONLY WITHOUT EXCEPTION. Every restatement found: 'no write capability of any kind … read-only without exception' (L9966); 'A normal support session is read-only without exception; no write capability exists inside it. A data repair is not support.' (L16022); 'no write operation of any kind is reachable inside a normal support session' (L18865); AC-SA-15-01 'for any account including the root' (L45832); 'Support reads only' (L48721); AC-WF-PLT-001-01 (L55012); L57962; L64640; AC-SEC-802 'on any path' (L104317); AC-4871 'every mutating control is absent rather than disabled-with-a-tooltip' (L107884); AC-51-09 'attempts are refused and audited' (L112819); L23771; L29168 'Support access is read-only at V1'; L34/L112436.
findings.bindingOn: Session capability grant; support-session UI and endpoints

findings.claim: DATA REPAIR IS NOT SUPPORT — the escalation rule. 'a data repair is not support and requires the compliance-emergency path' (L9718); 'perform a data repair — a data repair is not support' (L18786); 'a data repair is not support — anything that changes tenant data goes through the compliance-emergency path' (L23771); 'A data repair goes through the compliance-emergency path, which requires the root and one Admin' (L48721); 'A data repair is not support: … which Support cannot open' (L57962); 'no write inside a normal session: no configuration change, no record edit, no data repair' (L107819); L65407 'a data repair is explicitly not support'.

Escalation mechanics when a repair is needed: WF-SA-ESCALATE-TO-EMERGENCY — 'handed to the compliance-emergency path; no support session ever becomes a write session' (L16111). FB-SUPPORT-003: 'None — there is no fallback that grants write capability to a support session'; terminal safe state is 'A support engineer who can describe the fix and cannot perform it' (L64728). The banner control 'Grant the engineer write access' DOES NOT EXIST (L64699). Support cannot open the emergency path itself (L16099, L20741, L57962).

Write-attempt handling inside a support session: FAIL-14-07 — the write is refused at the session boundary; repeated refusals are visible through the tenant banner, the mirrored audit entries and the console-side action count; tenant data unchanged; the ticket stays open (L18854). FB-ROLE-010 / L58207: if a write path is ever reachable, first fallback is server-side write refusal regardless of path, escalating to suspending ALL support sessions platform-wide; recovery reconciliation compares support-session actions against write events, expected count ZERO (L55783, L58207). The storyboard SB-022 lists 'refused write attempt' as a Platform Access History line item (L64632).

Support session time bounds: default two-hour time box, stated at L21442, L30805, L45832, L47105-area, L55012, L64448, L72755, L87560, L107819, L117906. AC-SA-15-03: 'Sessions expire at their time box, default two hours, and cannot be extended in place.' The default is 'configurable in platform settings' (L16099) / 'configurable' (L23771).

NO IN-PLACE EXTENSION of a support session: AC-WF-ROLE-024-01 'No in-place extension of a support session; overruns are recorded' (L56107); AC-UC-PSUP-03-01 'One tenant per session; no in-place extension; actions never exceed the declared scope' (L58022); Support may_not 'extend a session in place' (L57962). WF-ROLE-024 terminal state: 'the session ends, and any period beyond the box is recorded as an overrun for investigation' (L56099).

Support session termination — three ways it ends: engineer close, tenant End-session press, or time-box expiry (L16111, L21439, L29208 states ended_by_tenant / ended_by_engineer / ended_by_time_box, L97121, L107825). WF-SA-CLOSE-SESSION terminal state: 'session-ended event mirrored to both audit streams' (L16111).

What the tenant sees and can do — support session: a persistent banner naming the ENGINEER and the START TIME renders for the whole session with a working End-session control (AC-SA-15-04, L45832). Fixed banner text: 'Platform support is viewing your tenant. Started [time]. Engineer [name]. End session [button]' (L64640, is_hard_gate false). The End-session control belongs to the tenant and is deliberately available to ANY signed-in tenant web user, not only the Tenant Admin (L29199, L45700, L23599). A tenant user may NOT dismiss or hide the banner while the session is open (L29199).

Tenant termination is immediate and unconditional: AC-SA-15-05 'Pressing End session terminates platform access immediately' (L45832); AC-WF-ROLE-023-01 and AC-UC-PSUP-08-01 'immediate and unconditional; a failed termination is recorded, not hidden' (L56085, L58135); AC-SEC-804 'terminates a support session immediately and the termination is audited' (L104319); Support may_not 'refuse or delay a tenant termination' (L57962). If the timer fails, the tenant's End-session control still closes it (L117968).

NO BANNER MEANS NO SESSION (visibility as precondition, not decoration): 'No tenant record is read while the tenant cannot see that it is being read; if the banner cannot render, the session is suspended and no further reads are served until the banner is confirmed visible' (L14887); 'the session does not open, or terminates, if the banner cannot be shown — visibility is a precondition of the access rather than a decoration on it' (L64726); AC-4870 'No read of tenant operational content occurs before the tenant banner is confirmed displayed and the session-open event is committed to the tenant's audit stream' (L107883).

Support session scope constraints: ONE TENANT PER SESSION; actions never exceed the declared scope; Support may_not 'read a second tenant in one session' or 'issue any command from a support session' (L58022, L57962). Session scope is fixed at open and is NOT recomputed from role; no open session gains write capability if the operator's role changes mid-session (AC-UC-PSUP-14-01, L58249). Support's default scope is 'no tenant context at all; tenant context exists only while a session is open' (L16099).
findings.bindingOn: Server-side scope enforcement independent of the interface

findings.claim: Support session cannot enter a compliance-suspended tenant: 'a compliance-suspended tenant cannot be entered by a normal support session at all' (L70666); Support may_not 'enter a compliance-suspended tenant' (L16099, L23771, L54626, L57962, L104199). AC-SA-09-08: 'The only platform-side entry into a compliance-suspended tenant is the dual-authorised compliance-emergency path' (L45099).
findings.bindingOn: Support access machinery; OBJ-TENANT compliance suspension

findings.claim: Other things a support session cannot do (enumerated may_not): take a tenant quality decision; release a hold, approve a Job, decide a Lane B proposal, mark evidence reviewed, grant a qualification clearance, or resolve a sync conflict; own any configuration change of any kind; configure alerts (Support is a recipient, never a configurer); act as a tenant role; release a Severity 1 hold; suppress or hide the banner (L107819, L16099). Support also may_not 'Inspect a full trace' (L42715).

CLASS 2 — COMPLIANCE-EMERGENCY PATH, who may open it: Root Super Admin PLUS one platform Admin. Two distinct authorising identities, one of which is the root; neither alone opens it; it cannot be initiated by one person and cannot be reduced to one (AC-SA-15-07 L45832; AC-30D-1003 L74639; AC-SA-07-05-03 L44236; AC-SEC-803 L104318; L19688; L19777; L23852). Root 'co-authorise the compliance-emergency path with one Admin' (L15396); Admin 'second authorisation' (L23666, L103431).

Compliance-emergency path is THE ONLY WRITE ROUTE into tenant data from the platform side, and the only entry into a compliance-suspended tenant (L9737, L14780, L19781, AC-TIER-024 L12179, AC-SA-15-10 L45832, L64767, L109362, L112748, L21302). It is also the only re-entry route after compliance suspension (L81024, L81564, L113510, AC-WF-PLT-005-01 L55162).

Compliance-emergency scope discipline: a NAMED EMERGENCY CLASS plus a declared scope, declared BEFORE the session opens and never widened during it (AC-SA-15-08 L45832; L19777; L55049; L64767). Access outside the declared scope is 'refused and recorded, not merely logged as a warning; widening requires a new request with new authorisations, never an in-session widening' (L64858, FB-EMERG-004). The 'Open' control is inactive until named emergency class, declared scope and time box are supplied (L104252) and activates only when both authorisation slots are filled (L19760). The root may 'Narrow the declared scope before authorising' (L64827).
findings.bindingOn: Emergency session scope declaration; PER-SA-EMERGENCY-WRITE scope check

findings.claim: Authorisations are re-evaluated AT SESSION OPEN, not only at authorisation time; a revoked authorisation can never open a compliance-emergency session (AC-UC-PADM-17-01, L57519).

Compliance-emergency TIME BOX IS NOT FIXED BY THE SOURCE. It is stated as 'time-boxed' (L1498, L64767) but the two-hour default belongs to NORMAL SUPPORT SESSIONS ONLY — DEC-SEC-017 is 'New — Client Decision Required' for the emergency default (L104216), and DEC-SCHED-003 asks the same (L98699). Only recommendations exist: TRN-BG-03 recommends a 1-hour box 'shorter than the 2-hour support default because the capability is greater' (Recommendation - R&D, L19733), and TRN-BG-01 recommends a 4-hour request lapse period (L19731). One illustrative example opens for 60 minutes (L74624).
findings.bindingOn: Emergency session lease — DO NOT hard-code a default

findings.claim: Compliance-emergency close and tenant report: an AUTOMATIC post-session report is generated for the tenant on every close, INCLUDING a close by time-box expiry (L19780); 'the control to suppress the tenant report does not exist' (L64828). If report generation fails: regenerate, then escalate to the root with the raw action log for manual issuance; the session is closed, write access revoked, and the outstanding report obligation is a tracked open item visible in both streams — 'never quietly dropped' (FB-PLT-002 L55045, FB-ROLE-026 L56149, WF-ROLE-026 L56144). FB-EMERG-002 adds that the mirrored audit events remain queryable in the tenant's own log meanwhile (L64860).

When the second authorisation cannot be obtained the emergency simply does not happen: 'The compliance-emergency path cannot open on one authorisation; no fallback to single authorisation exists and none may be created' (FAIL-15-07 L19766); 'the dual-control requirement is never relaxed under time pressure' (FB-ROLE-025 L56126); terminal safe state 'No emergency session, preserving the dual-authorisation control' (FB-EMERG-001 L64856); 'If the two authorisations are not obtainable, no access occurs' (L1498). Remaining options are the read-only support session and layer-one telemetry (L64856).

Hard limits that bind even the compliance-emergency path: no platform role can perform any of the ten Command Center operational actions in any tenant in ANY access class, including the compliance-emergency path (AC-4874 L107887); no evidence record can be mutated or deleted on any surface including through the compliance-emergency path, 'which writes rather than erases' (AC-UC-DENY-18-01 L60675); the platform does not release tenant quality holds under any access class (L85170); no console role can write a tenant qualification outside the compliance-emergency path (AC-UC-ROOT-15-01 L57082); compliance suspension itself has deliberately NO emergency bypass of root approval (FB-SUSP-006 L65323); the emergency path is 'not a multi-factor bypass' (FB-AUTH-003 L82953) and 'not a convenience route for a locked-out Tenant Admin' (FB-HUMAN-004 L84636); the approval service being down does not create a bypass — the emergency path with its two authorisations is the available action (FB-ADM-01 L72805).

CLASS 3 — JBS ACCESS GRANT, standing access prohibited. 'JBS holds no standing access to any tenant workspace or to the console by default' (AC-PROD-020 L1500); 'Standing JBS access is Explicitly prohibited; every JBS touch is a scoped, time-boxed, reason-linked, audited and mirrored grant that expires' (L4627); AC-16-11 (L20139); AC-SA-16-01 'no default grant exists in any environment' (L45938); AC-SEC-807 (L104322); L117331. 'Employment by JBS, by the client, or by an implementation partner never confers permanent access. Every crossing is granted, exercised, and expires.' (L14790).

JBS grant issuance: grants are APPROVABLE OBJECTS under the change-approval discipline (L107819, L55089, L55072). Root 'approve JBS access grants' (L15396). The 23.16 workflow assigns Admin=drafts, Root Super Admin=approves and issues (L45848). AC-SA-16-02: every grant enumerates its scope, carries a time box, and links a reason BEFORE it can be submitted (L45938). Scope is 'by named modules or tenants' (L45890, L45875). Revocation control allowed to Root Super Admin and Admin, taking effect immediately (L45871, WF-ROLE-030 L56233).

JBS grant approval CLASS IS UNDECIDED: DEC-JBSAUTH-001 asks whether granting JBS access is an Admin routine action or a critical-class action; recommendation is 'Admin action for a new grant and critical class for an extension of an existing grant' — status open (L23081, index hits L21098/L21173/L21224).
findings.bindingOn: MTX-PLAT-02 MOD-SA-16; MTX-PLAT-13 JBS grant row

findings.claim: JBS grant scope of reach: 'into the console and, where needed, into tenant context' (L45875); JBS may 'exercise an access grant scoped to named modules or tenants, time-boxed, reason-linked, fully audited, and mirrored into the affected tenant's audit trail' and may 'change platform configuration under the change-approval discipline within the granted scope' (L107819). JBS may_not: hold standing access, write tenant data, enter a compliance-suspended tenant, browse ambiently, release a lot hold, approve a Job, or decide a Lane B proposal (L107819); may_not access outside granted scope or after expiry, and may_not hold root custody (L55072, AC-SA-16-06 L45938, L104203).

JBS grant expiry and failure handling: 'an expired grant never extends itself' — on mid-task expiry, request a fresh scoped grant, else the client's own platform team performs the work (FB-PLT-003 L55080). A grant committing with no time box is rejected at validation, and reconciliation must list grants with no expiry as ZERO (FB-ROLE-027 L56171). A session opening broader than granted is stopped by server-side scope enforcement independent of the interface, escalating to terminating all JBS sessions (FB-ROLE-028 L56194). If the expiry job does not run: expire on next pass, then revoke explicitly; reconciliation reports grants exercised past expiry, which must be ZERO (FB-ROLE-029 L56216, WF-ROLE-029 L56211). If an open session survives revocation: force session termination, then disable the grantee's console account (FB-ROLE-030 L56238). Illustrative grant time box: 5 working days (L45873).

AUDIT STREAMS — the dual-write rule for ALL THREE classes. 'Every cross-boundary access is written twice: once in the platform audit and once mirrored into the tenant's audit stream, IN THE SAME TRANSACTION. If the mirror write fails, the session action is refused.' (L14886). Every platform-side access event appears in the tenant's own audit stream AND in the tenant's Platform Access History screen (L6983, AC-PROD-022 L1500, AC-SA-18-05 L46193, AC-SEC-103 L103328 'from the moment the session opens'). Mirroring is CONTINUOUS during a session, not at close (AC-30D-1004 L74640). 'One audit truth per tenant' (L70695, L110975 — the tenant-facing Platform Access History reads the same records rather than a separate summary).
findings.bindingOn: Session service one-transaction mirror guarantee; audit subsystem

findings.claim: Per-class audit event typing: the JBS session carries its 'own named platform audit event class' (OBJ-SA-JBSSESSION L45890, OBJ-081 L9753, L55072, L55089); the compliance-emergency session carries 'emergency-grade audit flags' plus OBJ-SA-POSTREPORT (L45772). AC-4873: all three access classes appear IDENTICALLY in the tenant's Platform Access History and 'no filter or export can omit a class' (L107886); L29166 says the same via FUNC-DOH-13-1.1.2; L97134 'Lists all three platform-side access classes identically'.
findings.bindingOn: Platform Access History; audit event classes

findings.claim: Platform Access History fields the tenant sees: access class, actor, start time, end time, reason class, ticket reference, action count, End-session control (L64450). Console-side session list carries who, tenant, reason, scope, expiry and action count with per-session detail (L54979, L55009, L58038, L58020). Reconciliation compares console session actions against tenant-mirrored action counts and raises any discrepancy as a finding (L16125, L14880, L55783, L56059).

Mirroring failure = access stops, including for the emergency path. FB-RBAC-06: where the mirror write fails the session does not open; an already-open session terminates immediately and the partial access is recorded on both sides with an explicit gap marker; where neither mirroring nor banner rendering can be restored, no session may open and support work proceeds through layer-one telemetry only; terminal safe state — 'Every layer-three access is blocked including the compliance-emergency path' (L21453). FB-SUP-001 says the same at the SURF-SA side and adds 'terminate a live session that loses mirroring, recording actions taken before the loss, and notify the tenant' (L107877). FB-BOUNDARY-001 / FB-SUP-001: a failed session is NEVER resumed — a new session is opened with a fresh reason (L14880, L16125). FB-GOV-001: 'a session that cannot be mirrored cannot open' (L9959). FB-SA-05 (L42862).

WHAT 'NO AMBIENT BROWSING' EXCLUDES — the positive statement of what remains reachable WITHOUT a named class is the three-layer data-access model, closed at three layers: Layer one, administration and telemetry — metadata, counts, rates, statuses, NEVER operational content; Layer two, comparative cross-tenant analytics — ANONYMISED AGGREGATES enforced as an invariant; Layer three, record-level operational content — reached ONLY through a named, audited, session-scoped access class (L21378, restated L54954, L72757, L109381, L103228).
findings.bindingOn: Per-read enforcement on all console reads

findings.claim: 'No ambient browsing' is enforced at route/API level, not only in the UI: enforcement points named are the console gateway and every tenant-content read path (L14777), console route enumeration (L9965), console routing + server (L72755), console authorisation layer (L54952), and layer-three access gate (AC-RBAC-321 L21484). AC-SEC-801: 'no fourth path into tenant record-level content is reachable from ANY console screen or API' (L104316, TEST-SEC-801). AC-SA-000-07: 'No console screen outside a named access session renders record-level operational content for any tenant' (L42885). AC-SA-INV-002 (L47848). AC-UC-DENY-11-01 binds 'all four platform roles including the root' (L60549). AC-AUTH-006: 'Platform console roles hold no tenant operational authority outside a named access class' (L10429, TEST-AUTH-006). AC-SA-005 / TEST-SA-004 (L11710). AC-30D-1001 (L74637).
findings.bindingOn: Console routes and APIs; TEST-SEC-801, TEST-SA-004, TEST-AUTH-006

findings.claim: 'No ambient browsing' explicitly covers observability and exports: AC-4801 — 'No observability view, alert, dashboard, or export in the platform console exposes record-level operational content outside a support session, the compliance-emergency path, or a JBS access grant' (L107297). AC-AI-013-4 — 'every record-level access opens a named, reason-required, audited session mirrored to the tenant' (L87648). AC-AI-008-4 — no query path can return another tenant's memory 'including under failover, cache, index, or SUPPORT-SESSION conditions' (L87062). Reads are audited only where the source requires it, inside the three named classes; general read auditing is deliberately NOT invented (L74046).
findings.bindingOn: Observability views, exports, memory query layer

findings.claim: Ambient-browsing detection/response: FUNC-SA-AMBIENT-ATTEMPT is a named function of MOD-SA-15 (L60870). FB-PLATSURF-001 — if a console screen renders tenant operational content outside a session, or a session frame exposes navigation to a second tenant: withhold the response and refuse the request; then terminate the session and DISABLE the console screen pending investigation; 'cross-tenant exposure is treated as a security incident, never as a rendering defect' (L16240). FB-GLO-01 — any chapter describing a platform touch that is none of the three named classes is reclassified into one of the three or removed (L6285).

Non-human identities are bound by the same closure: 'No non-human identity may cross a tenant boundary except where the source explicitly makes the component cross-tenant, and then only on anonymised aggregates or within a named, audited, session-scoped access class' — ENFORCED platform invariant, locked with no off position (L18107). The support-tool identity IDENT-SUPTOOL 'cannot be used outside an open session and dies at session end' (L18865). Scheduler Controller and Execution Worker may_not 'hold ambient authority'; the Controller may_not read tenant operational content at all (L109421). Platform Engineer may 'replay a dead-lettered occurrence only through a named access class' (L109174).
findings.bindingOn: All non-human identities; IDENT-SUPTOOL, IDENT-SCHED-CTRL, IDENT-SCHED-WORK

findings.claim: No impersonation / no acting-as-role: AC-SEC-806 — 'No platform operator ever acts under a tenant user's identity; every action names the operator' (L104321, TEST-SEC-805). 'Nothing hidden means: no privileged exemption, no silent path, no acting-as-role fiction, and no one-sided visibility' (L73978). Support may_not 'act as a tenant role' (L16099). No tenant role can authenticate to the console under any configuration, including during any of the three classes (AC-SA-000-01 L42879).

THE EIGHT ACCESS CLASSES FOR A SURFACE are a DIFFERENT and unrelated vocabulary from the three named platform access classes. The extract carries the eight only as an ordered list (L16178 for platform-role reach across the five surfaces; L17213 reusing it 'from section 11.6' for tenant roles across the five surfaces). NO per-class definition of Direct / Read-only / Masked / Diagnostic-only / Action-only / Temporarily elevated / Tenant-approved / Prohibited appears anywhere in the extract, and NO passage maps the eight onto the three. Any mapping is an inference the source does not make.
findings.bindingOn: Every module screen that renders a role-by-surface authority cell

findings.claim: Only fragmentary usage of the eight-class tokens survives in the extract, and it is all TENANT-side: Tenant Admin 'Direct — configuration, users, roles, tenant administration area', 'Action-only in the Studio', 'Action-only in the Command Center', 'Prohibited on drafts and on every approval stage in the Studio', 'Prohibited on the Super Admin platform console'; Supervisor 'Direct in the Hub / Studio / Command Center', 'Action-only on the Frontline — second-identity step-up for sign-off', 'Read-only on the sync-conflict panel' (L17261, L17262). A 'Diagnostic-only example' exists involving the Shift Handoff Agent producing an empty brief (L16219) but the example's content is not extracted. NO extracted entry uses Masked, Temporarily elevated, or Tenant-approved as an access class.
findings.bindingOn: Role-by-surface matrices — the eight tokens are underspecified in the extract

findings.claim: The nearest textual bridge from the eight to the three is the recurring phrase 'session-scoped elevation only' applied to Support on SURF-SA (L20741, L42715, L44714, L52401, L54626, L57962, L74224). That phrase resembles the 'Temporarily elevated' class token but the source never says so. Similarly DEC-CONSENT-001/DEC-SUPPORT-002 debate tenant consent, which resembles 'Tenant-approved', but no passage names the class. Treat both as UNSTATED.
findings.bindingOn: Do not derive the eight-to-three mapping in code or UI

findings.claim: A THIRD, separate closed vocabulary is easily confused with both: the permission-matrix cell status set (Allowed / Allowed with conditions / Read-only / Explicitly prohibited / Unavailable / …). Its membership itself varies by passage — 6 tokens (L1200), 9 tokens (L10238, L14234, L20811, L109073), 8 tokens (L67751, L81278, L85157), 7 tokens (L99306), 5 tokens as a 'partial closed set observed' (L61167). Rule stated everywhere: no matrix cell may be blank.

Grant identifiers for the three classes exist as fixtures: GRANT-SUP-01 (support session, L104199), GRANT-EMG-01 (compliance-emergency path, L104201), GRANT-JBS-01 (JBS access grant, L104203), collectively 'The three named platform access classes' (L104199). The unified session object 'Platform access session (three named classes)' carries states open / expired / administratively closed / tenant-ended and relates all three to the tenant audit stream and Platform Access History (L104197).

Console roles enumerated as bound by the closure: Root Super Admin (L1347, L11682, L15396, L65398, L76090, L97152, L117322), Admin (L2151, L23666, L65400, L97153, L103431, L117322), Platform Engineer (L20740, L65401, L91285, L117322), Support (L9718, L16099, L57962, L104199, L107819) — plus 'Every platform console role' (L72020) and 'client platform team' (L78166). No role, including the root, is exempt: root may_not 'browse tenant operational content ambiently' or 'write into tenant data outside the compliance-emergency path' (L15396).

Cross-tenant and memory reach for platform roles inside a class remains restricted: Root/Admin — 'Cross-tenant aggregates: Read-only, anonymised'; 'Tenant memory content: Unavailable — counts and volume only'; 'Another tenant's data: Explicitly prohibited without a named access class PER TENANT' (L97152, L97153). Support — 'Tenant memory content: Unavailable', 'Cross-tenant aggregates: Unavailable', 'Another tenant's data: Explicitly prohibited' (L97155). Platform roles may not de-anonymise or disable cross-tenant analytics anonymisation (L97152).

Recorded EXTRACTION GAPS (identifiers referenced by a numbered series but absent from the extract, so their text is unknown here): AC-SA-15-06 and AC-SA-15-09 are missing from the AC-SA-15-01..11 series at L45832; AC-SA-16-03, -04, -05 and -07 are missing from the AC-SA-16 series at L45938; AC-SEC-805 is missing from the AC-SEC-801..807 series at L104316-104322. AC-ACCESS-1001..1009 and TEST-ACCESS-1001..1009 are indexed at L14636-14644 and L14648-14656 but their statements are not carried in the extract. Do not assume these are absent from the source.

'8' is a SOURCE-CLOSED count of per-surface access classes, stated twice. Neither is an extracted-identifier tally. By contrast, the extract-wide counts (2964 business_rules, 530 roles_rules, 1190 state_vocabularies, 566 contradictions, etc. per registries/generated/source-reconciliation.json totals) are EXTRACTION counts across 36 chunks with heavy duplication — e.g. the single 'three access classes' rule appears as ~20 separate business_rules entries. Never present an extraction count as a canonical inventory.
