closedSets.name: The three named platform access classes (platform-side reach into record-level tenant operational content)
The eight access classes for a surface (role reach across the five surfaces)
The three-layer platform data-access model (what is reachable without an access class)
members: Layer one — administration and telemetry: metadata, counts, rates, statuses, never operational content
Layer two — comparative cross-tenant analytics: anonymised aggregates, enforced as an invariant
Layer three — record-level operational content: only through a named, audited, session-scoped access class

closedSets.name: Ways a normal support session ends
members: ended by the tenant from the banner

closedSets.name: Authorisations required to open the compliance-emergency path
Grant fixture identifiers for the three classes
Support session lifecycle (the nine-state enumeration; competing shorter enumerations exist — see contradictions)
Critical-class actions requiring Root approval (context: compliance suspension sits here; JBS-grant class placement is undecided per DEC-JBSAUTH-001)

contradictions: PLATFORM ENGINEER AND SUPPORT SESSIONS — DIRECT CONFLICT, no governing decision recorded. L20740 lists Platform Engineer may_not 'Enter tenant context under any access class' and may_not 'Open a support session'. L65401 lists Platform Engineer may 'Open a read-only support session (Allowed with conditions)'. L117322 lists Platform Engineer may 'open a read-only support session' and 'read record-level tenant operational content through a named access class'. L45757 and L116399 include Platform Engineer in MOD-SA-15 roles_allowed; L21092, L11672, L60870, L76178, L98243 exclude it. Record BOTH; do not pick one.

BANNER-RENDER FAILURE — three incompatible resolutions. (a) L14887: the session is SUSPENDED and no further reads served until the banner is confirmed visible. (b) L64726 / L107883 / AC-4870: the session DOES NOT OPEN, or terminates; no read occurs before the banner is confirmed displayed. (c) FB-SEQ-028 at L70722 states the source does NOT specify this and its terminal safe state is that 'visibility is delayed rather than lost' with the session left running to its time box — the opposite of (b). DEC-SUPPORTVIS-001 (L70722) is open with three options (terminate automatically / block opening until confirmed / accept audit-only visibility), recommendation = block opening. FB-ROLE-022 (L56059) and FB-SUP-001 (L16125) add a fourth shape: re-render, then terminate.

END-SESSION CONTROL ACROSS THE THREE CLASSES — DEC-EMEREND-001 open (L14878, L17364). §8.15.1 attaches the banner and End-session control explicitly to the NORMAL SUPPORT SESSION only and says nothing about the other two classes. Against this: L64810 states as a hard gate that 'No End-session control is offered for the compliance-emergency class, because an emergency access the tenant could terminate would not be an emergency access'; L51712 states a MOD-DOH-13 End-session control whose effect is 'Ends an in-session support OR COMPLIANCE-EMERGENCY access session'; L16512-area MOD-DOH-13 descriptions name only the support-session banner. Recommended (not adopted) position at L14878: banner on all three, End-session on the support session and the JBS grant but NOT the emergency path, with the post-session report as compensating visibility.

JBS GRANT WRITE CAPABILITY — DEC-JBSWRITE-001 / DEC-HO-JBSWRITE-001, unresolved (L14877, L17363, L23833, L25443, L74630). §8.16 places JBS access under 'exactly the same discipline' as the other classes while §8.15.2 says the compliance-emergency path is 'the ONLY one with write capability'; §8.8.5 nevertheless contemplates JBS authoring capacity that writes. L74630 records it plainly: 'the source states the grant is scoped without enumerating write capability'. Meanwhile L107819 lists JBS may 'change platform configuration under the change-approval discipline within the granted scope' while may_not 'write tenant data'. Recommendation (not adopted): read-only always, because it keeps §8.15.2's 'only one' literally true.

A POSSIBLE FOURTH WRITE PATH — DEC-ACCESS-001, both readings preserved (L104209). §8.15.2's 'only write path' claim collides with §8.8.5 provisioning onboarding implementation staff an author-and-submit role inside the tenant workspace (OBJ-SA-IMPLROLE L44793, GRANT-IMPL-AUTHOR L75446, L30828). Reading A: a tenant-granted role held by a platform-side person, therefore tenant-side access. Reading B: a fourth write path into tenant data needing an exception clause or a fourth named class. Unresolved — 'Leaves one write path into tenant data unresolved.'

IMPERSONATION — DEC-IMPERSONATE-001 / DEC-ACCESS-002, unresolved (L17647, L104207). §4.12.3/§4.12.4 lists 'cross-tenant visibility and impersonation control' while Part VIII defines no impersonation feature, states support is read-only without exception, closes access classes at three, forbids an acting-as-role record, and asserts AC-SEC-806 (L104321). Reading 1: the phrase names the guardrail that PREVENTS impersonation. Reading 2: it names a control panel for an impersonation FEATURE, which would imply a fourth named access class with dual authorisation, tenant banner and tenant-side mirroring. Blueprint's Derived Clarification reads V1 as having no user impersonation, but both readings are preserved.

TRACE VIEWER AS AN AMBIENT-BROWSING PATH — DEC-SEC-020, New/Client Decision Required (L104506, L106643). The Trace Viewer is a SURF-SA module exposing full orchestrator reasoning traces (roles Platform Engineer, Admin, Root Super Admin) and traces 'may contain tenant operational content, retained 24 months'. Option A: trace access sits behind an access class as layer-3 content. Option B: a console module with no access-class qualification. Stated impact: 'Otherwise the trace viewer becomes the ambient-browsing path the source forbids.' Note the collision with L42715, which lists Support may_not 'Inspect a full trace' — the restriction is currently expressed as a role rule, not an access-class rule.

ROOT AS 'UNRESTRICTED' — L14322. §8.8.1 describes the root account as having 'unrestricted access to both bands' and then immediately constrains it with the six invariants, the evaluation gate and the three-layer access boundary (§3.1, §8.1.2, §8.15). No governing decision recorded. Implementers must not read 'unrestricted' as an access-class exemption: L15396 and AC-SA-15-01 (L45832) explicitly bind the root.

SESSION-OPENING AUTHORITY — DEC-HO-SUPGRANT-001, Client Decision Required (L23773, L25442). The source does not state whether a support session is opened SELF-SERVICE by Support against a valid ticket, or requires an Admin grant per session or per tenant. Options recorded: self-service against a ticket / per-tenant standing grant / per-session Admin grant. FB-ROLE-013 (L55850) assumes a self-service-shaped flow by making 'an Admin opens a read-only session under the same discipline' the fallback when the identity provider is unavailable.

SUPPORT SESSION STATE ENUMERATION — at least six incompatible enumerations, all authoritative-sounding: 5 states 'opened/suspended/terminated/expired/closed' (L14779); 4 states 'requested/open/ended by the tenant/expired' OBJ-079 (L9715); 8 states 'requested/open/active/ended by tenant/expired/closed by operator/mirrored/reported' OBJ-SA-SESSION (L45772-45773); 5 states 'opened/closed/expired/terminated by the tenant/overrun' (L55009); 3 states 'open/expired/tenant-terminated' (L58020); 4 states 'none/open/terminated by tenant/closed' (L64680); 9 states 'Requested/Validating/Open/Refused/EndedByEngineer/EndedByTenant/Expired/VisibilityDegraded/Recorded' (L70757); plus the shared 'open/expired/administratively closed/tenant-ended' (L104197). No passage reconciles them.

COMPLIANCE-EMERGENCY SESSION STATE ENUMERATION — four incompatible enumerations: 'requested/dual-authorised/open/closed/reported' OBJ-080 (L9734); 'Requested/Authorised/Open/Acting/Closed/Reported' OBJ-EMERGSESSION (L19731); 'requested/open/active/expired/closed/mirrored/reported' OBJ-SA-EMERGENCYSESSION (L45772); 'none/pending second authorisation/open/closed' (L64808).

JBS GRANT STATE ENUMERATION — four incompatible enumerations: 'requested/approved/active/expired' OBJ-JBS-GRANT (L4652); 'requested/approved/active/expired/revoked' OBJ-081 (L9753, L9761); 'drafted/pending approval/issued/active/expired/revoked/reconciled' OBJ-SA-JBSGRANT (L45890-45891); 'NoAccess/GrantRequested/GrantApproved/Exercised/Expired/Revoked' (L55089).

PLATFORM ACCESS HISTORY OWNERSHIP AND AUDIENCE — module id given as MOD-DOH-13 (L1476, L11141, L14789, L22019, L25969, L47264) and as MOD-DOH-11 (L97134). Its roles_allowed differ by passage: {Tenant Admin} (L11141); {Tenant Admin, Read-only Auditor} (L14789, L25969, L47264, L97134); {Tenant Admin, Supervisor, Quality Manager, Read-only Auditor} (L22019); {Tenant Admin, Quality Manager, Read-only Auditor} (L64450). The End-session control's holder is likewise contested: 'Tenant Admin' (L44272, L74587, L87560, L23599) versus 'any tenant user seeing the banner' / 'any signed-in tenant web user' stated as a deliberate design choice (L29199, L45700).

MOD-SA-15 SCOPE — whether the compliance-emergency path lives inside MOD-SA-15 or beside it. L45757 states MOD-SA-15's purpose as providing BOTH 'the read-only support session and the separate compliance-emergency path', and SCR-SA-22 (emergency initiation) is assigned module_id MOD-SA-15 (L42814, L45753); L2442, L11672, L60870, L76178 describe MOD-SA-15 as support sessions only. MOD-SA-16 is likewise described twice with different purpose and roles: 'grants into the console and, where needed, into tenant context' with five role groups (L45875) versus 'The JBS platform access class' with {Root Super Admin, Support} (L60871).

PERMISSION-MATRIX CELL STATUS SET — the closed set's own membership is contested across passages: 6 tokens (L1200), 9 tokens (L10238, L14234, L20811, L109073), 8 tokens (L67751, L81278, L85157), 7 tokens (L99306), 5 tokens declared a 'partial closed set observed' (L61167). This vocabulary is distinct from both the three named access classes and the eight per-surface access classes and must not be conflated with either.

EXPORT FROM INSIDE A SESSION — unresolved and materially affects the audit story. DEC-SUPEXP-001 (L16123, L17370) is open; the recommendation is NO export, with findings written in prose, 'keeping tenant operational content inside the platform where the mirroring holds'. Until decided, an export feature would remove tenant operational content into a ticketing system the tenant cannot see — effectively defeating the mirroring guarantee at L14886.

value.topic: SURF-SA cross-cutting spine: the six ENFORCED platform invariants (evaluation gate, sandbox-before-publish, encryption at rest, encryption in transit, cross-tenant analytics anonymisation, one-transaction audit guarantee) — what each forbids, where each renders, what "locked with no off position for any account including the root" means in the UI, and what happens on an attempt

findings.claim: SET AND ORDER. The source enumerates the six invariants in a stable canonical order at every enumeration point: evaluation gate; sandbox-before-publish; encryption at rest; encryption in transit; cross-tenant analytics anonymisation; one-transaction audit guarantee. No passage reorders them. What DOES vary is the label and the article: 'The six invariants' (L2143), 'The six enforced invariants rendered locked' (L12098), 'The six platform invariants' (L14944), 'The six ENFORCED platform invariants' (L21017), 'The six enforced invariants (ENFORCED badge, locked)' (L54626), 'The six ENFORCED invariants' (L66460), and at L84761/L108617 the definite articles are dropped ('evaluation gate', 'one-transaction audit guarantee').
findings.bindingOn: Every console account on SURF-SA including ROLE-PLAT-ROOT; asserted platform-wide

findings.claim: The set is CLOSED AT SIX and the count is restated as a numeric fact in at least ten independent places, always as 6/'six', never more and never fewer.

NUMBERED RESTATEMENT. The invariant set is 'Absolute rule 11': the six bind every account including the root and have 'no off position and no approval path around them'. Enforcement point given as 'Settings render locked; no approval path exists'.

WHAT 'NO OFF POSITION' MEANS, STATEMENT 1 — no control exists at all. AC-SA-INV-003: none of the six 'has an off control, an approval path, or a configuration key on any screen, for any account including the root'. This is three separate absences: no toggle, no approval route, no config key.
findings.bindingOn: Platform settings, all screens, all accounts

findings.claim: WHAT 'NO OFF POSITION' MEANS, STATEMENT 2 — the absence is the rendering. AC-RBAC-304: the six 'present no off control to any account, and a direct application programming interface attempt to disable one denies and is audited'. Enforcement point is stated as BOTH 'Platform settings and service layer' — interface and service.
findings.bindingOn: All console accounts and all direct API callers

findings.claim: WHAT 'NO OFF POSITION' MEANS, STATEMENT 3 — refusal is server-side and independent of the interface. AC-UC-DENY-20-01: 'All six invariants refuse every account including the root, through the interface and directly', enforcement point 'server-side refusal independent of the interface'. AC-WF-ROLE-004-01 repeats this at the 'settings write endpoint'. Implementers must not rely on UI suppression alone.
findings.bindingOn: Settings write endpoint; every account including root

findings.claim: UI RENDERING — ENFORCED badge. The invariants render with an 'ENFORCED badge with lock icon' on MOD-SA-07, effect 'Renders an invariant as locked with no approval path; edits refused and audited'. Restated as 'ENFORCED badge' rendering each of the six 'locked with no control for any account'.

UI RENDERING — the approval control itself is dead. On the approval queue the control 'Approve anything touching the six enforced invariants' is 'Disabled — no approval path exists for any account'. There is therefore no maker-checker route to an invariant change.
findings.bindingOn: Approval queue (SCR-SA-10 in the CHK-015 numbering); Admin and Root Super Admin

findings.claim: WHAT HAPPENS ON AN ATTEMPT — canonical rule. AC-SA-000-05: 'Any attempt to change one of the six enforced invariants fails for every account including the root, and the attempt is written to the platform audit log as an attempt on a locked setting.' Enforcement point: 'Platform Settings, locked rendering'.

WHAT HAPPENS ON AN ATTEMPT — the audit class. AC-SEC-602: 'An attempt to change a locked setting produces an audit event of the locked-setting-attempt class.' 'Attempts on locked settings' is named as one of the platform audit log's named event classes.

WHAT HAPPENS ON AN ATTEMPT — refusal survives the approver. A platform change 'from proposal to effect' has the terminal state 'Rejected regardless of approver, including the root, where an enforced invariant would be breached'.
findings.bindingOn: Platform Engineer maker / Admin or Root checker workflow

findings.claim: WHAT HAPPENS ON AN ATTEMPT — the settings workflow's own terminal state. 'A settings change from intent to effect' terminates as 'refused outright where the setting is one of the six enforced invariants' (versus 'applied with its audit event in one transaction' for a legal change).

THE INVARIANTS ARE A FEATURE-CONTROL KIND. 'Platform invariant' is one of the nine feature-control kinds, and it is step 1 — the first and highest-precedence step — of the fourteen-step effective-control evaluation order, ahead of the global kill switch, the AI emergency pause, the release flag and the eval-gate posture. Implementation consequence: the invariant check must run before every other control resolution.
findings.bindingOn: Feature-control record; every effective-control resolution on the platform

findings.claim: NOT SUSPENDABLE BY DEPLOYMENT. 'No deployment or migration may disable any of the six enforced invariants'; the deployment-conformance suite asserts all six; the pre-release parity suite asserts 'no identity shape, tenant configuration, suspension state, or caller class permits an action that would breach a platform floor or one of the six enforced invariants'.
findings.bindingOn: Deployment pipeline, release pipeline, all releases

findings.claim: NOT SUSPENDABLE BY DESIGN DRIFT. FB-COV-01 (§5.11 invariant erosion): a design chapter offering an administrative path around one of the six has the path removed and the invariant restated as locked; failing that it is referred to the client as a contract change 'because removing an invariant changes what the platform is'. Terminal safe state: 'The invariant stands and the requested capability is not built.'
findings.bindingOn: Design and specification process, not runtime

findings.claim: ROLE-LEVEL PROHIBITION IS UNIFORM ACROSS ALL FOUR CONSOLE ROLES. 'All four platform roles including the root' may_not 'disable the evaluation gate, sandbox-before-publish, encryption at rest, encryption in transit, cross-tenant analytics anonymisation, or the one-transaction audit guarantee', scope condition 'no approval path exists around the six enforced invariants'. Restated per-role for Root, Admin, Platform Engineer and Support ('Switch off an enforced invariant — Explicitly prohibited').

ROOT-SPECIFIC RESTATEMENTS. The Root Super Admin may_not list carries the invariant prohibition in at least fourteen separate role rows across the source, with varying verbs: 'disable' (L1347, L20738, L91288), 'turn off' (L9875, L84669), 'switch off' (L76090, L78327), 'escape' (L4619, L17835), 'bypass' (L23666), 'change' (L42712), 'disable or route around' (L15396).
findings.bindingOn: ROLE-PLAT-ROOT (exactly one account, backend-created, custody with the client)

findings.claim: EVALUATION GATE — WHAT IT FORBIDS. Enabling any atom, agent, capability or composed behaviour while any referenced/gating evaluation scenario is pending or failing, for every account including the root. Stated as 'Explicitly prohibited for every account'.
findings.bindingOn: Atom registration records, agent definitions, composed behaviours; every account

findings.claim: EVALUATION GATE — SCOPE EXTENSIONS. It also forbids: promoting a capability that FAILED its scenarios (AC-RBAC-331); publishing an unevaluated agent or composed behaviour via a scheduled occurrence; any version change forward or backward without the gate (AC-44A-16-1); substituting an alternate model on provider/model failover until the gate is re-asserted. Approval does not substitute for the gate.
findings.bindingOn: Agents, atoms, composed behaviours, model bindings, scheduled publication

findings.claim: EVALUATION GATE — THE ROOT CANNOT LAUNDER IT. The root specifically may_not 'mark a scenario as accepted' or 'remove a scenario' — closing the two obvious workarounds to a gate that cannot be switched off.

EVALUATION GATE — UI MEANING OF 'LOCKED'. The enablement control 'is not offered at all while a scenario fails' — the gate is expressed as the absence of the enable affordance, not as a greyed toggle. The capability state machine backs this: OBJ-CAPABILITY states are Enabled / DisableSubmitted / Disabled / EvalPending and 'no edge reaches Enabled without passing EvalPending'.
findings.bindingOn: Atom registry and agent enablement screens (MOD-SA-02, MOD-SA-03, MOD-SA-05)

findings.claim: EVALUATION GATE — WHERE RENDERED. SCR-SA-EVALGATE 'Evaluation gate view' (MOD-SA-05); SCR-SA-06 'Eval harness — scenarios, runs, gate view, drift canary'; storyboard SB-43-204 'The enforced gate, rendered — ENFORCED badge with no control to change it'; the control 'Disable the evaluation gate' is itself catalogued with effect 'Rendered locked — ENFORCED invariant, no account can switch it off'.

EVALUATION GATE — FAILS CLOSED WHEN THE HARNESS IS DOWN. FB-SA-06: eval harness unavailable → retry the run → refuse enablement → terminal safe state 'Enablement blocked — the gate fails closed and has no off position'; recovery records the blocked window and confirms no capability was enabled meanwhile.

EVALUATION GATE — ENFORCEMENT SIDE IS STATED. 'Specification gates are hard and always; the evaluation gate is hard and always including for the root account' with enforcement point 'On-device (spec, qualification) and server-side (evaluation)'. The evaluation gate is a server-side control, unlike the specification and qualification gates.
findings.bindingOn: All five surfaces, all nine human security role types

findings.claim: SANDBOX-BEFORE-PUBLISH — WHAT IT FORBIDS, narrowly. It is a publication gate only: no tenant-composed agent becomes available on any floor without the tenant's approval chain, this module's review decision, and 'passing sandbox evals' (AC-SA-03-04). Due-moment re-validation of scheduled activation covers 'sandbox evidence' as one of four checks.
findings.bindingOn: MOD-SA-03 composed-agent review queue; scheduled content activation

findings.claim: SANDBOX-BEFORE-PUBLISH — SOURCE IS OTHERWISE SILENT. Outside the six-item enumerations and the four lines above, the source never states what a sandbox run consists of, who executes it, what artefact constitutes 'sandbox evidence', or how it differs from an evaluation run. This is the least-specified of the six. Treat the implementation shape as unstated, not as inferable from the evaluation gate.

SANDBOX-BEFORE-PUBLISH — WHERE RENDERED. Paired with the evaluation gate under one ENFORCED badge: 'Renders the evaluation gate and sandbox-before-publish with no control to change them'. AC-SA-05-01: 'No account, including the root, can disable the eval gate or sandbox-before-publish, and both render as ENFORCED in Settings.'
findings.bindingOn: MOD-SA-05 / Platform Settings; Root Super Admin and Platform Engineer

findings.claim: ENCRYPTION AT REST AND IN TRANSIT — WHAT THEY FORBID. Switching either off, by any account including the root: 'switch off encryption at rest or in transit — ENFORCED invariants with no off position for any account including the root'. Restated in root role rows as 'disable encryption at rest or in transit'. Both are tied to the absolute-tenant-isolation clause: 'nothing is shared across tenants and nothing becomes external training data'.
findings.bindingOn: ROLE-PLAT-ROOT and all console roles; all surfaces

findings.claim: ENCRYPTION — RENDERING AND TEST. AC-SEC-601: 'Encryption at rest and encryption in transit render locked with the ENFORCED badge, with no control and no approval path, for every account including the root', enforcement point TEST-SEC-601 'invariant lock'. Rendered on SB-SEC-006-S1 'Super Admin Platform Settings — Memory and Data (ENFORCED locked rows)', where the badge effect is 'Renders encryption and anonymisation as locked; attempts are audited'.

ENCRYPTION AT REST — THE ONE OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE THE SOURCE SPELLS OUT. When a remote wipe cannot reach a device, 'encryption at rest is the operative control rather than the wipe'; the terminal safe state is a locked device with all local data preserved and still encrypted. This is the only place an invariant is given a load-bearing fallback role.
findings.bindingOn: SURF-FL devices under DEC-WIPE-001; approved by Root Super Admin under maker-checker

findings.claim: ENCRYPTION — THE MECHANISM IS AN OPEN CLIENT DECISION. DEC-SEC-014 'Key hierarchy, custody, rotation, and customer-managed keys' is status 'New — Client Decision Required' with no adopted position and explicitly 'no value proposed for rotation periods'. The invariant is locked but its cryptographic substance is undefined. Note also that the source specifies no algorithm, no TLS version and no mutual-authentication requirement anywhere for encryption in transit; the only place transport security is discussed as a control is DEC-PKGSIGN-001's rejected option 'no signing, relying on transport security alone'.
findings.bindingOn: Implementation team — blocking open decision under an otherwise locked invariant

findings.claim: CROSS-TENANT ANALYTICS ANONYMISATION — WHAT IT FORBIDS. De-anonymising a comparative view or distribution for any account including the root ('Comparative views are anonymised before aggregation and cannot be de-anonymised by any account including the root'); returning de-anonymised output under any configuration (AC-RBAC-324); rendering any tenant identifier in any console view that compares tenants (AC-SEC-101); and any operational content in any aggregate.
findings.bindingOn: Aggregation pipeline / query layer; MOD-SA-10; every account including root

findings.claim: CROSS-TENANT ANALYTICS ANONYMISATION — ORDERING IS THE INVARIANT. 'anonymisation precedes aggregation — enforced invariant' on OBJ-SA-DISTRIBUTION ('Anonymised comparative distribution (derived, never authored)'). Implementation consequence: anonymisation cannot be a presentation-layer mask applied after aggregation.

CROSS-TENANT ANALYTICS ANONYMISATION — PLACE IN THE ACCESS MODEL. It is Layer 2 of the three-layer data-access model, restated in four places with identical structure: Layer 1 administration/telemetry (metadata, counts, rates, statuses, never operational content); Layer 2 comparative cross-tenant analytics (anonymised aggregates, 'enforced as an invariant'); Layer 3 record-level operational content (only through a named, audited, session-scoped access class).

CROSS-TENANT ANALYTICS ANONYMISATION — DEGRADATION RULE. FB-SA-01: 'Where anonymisation cannot be guaranteed for a comparative view, the view renders unavailable rather than degrading to named data.' Terminal safe state is an unavailable measure — 'never a zero, never a blank', with an as-of timestamp (AC-SA-000-06).
findings.bindingOn: MOD-SA-10 rendering; SCR-SA-16 / tenant metrics screen

findings.claim: CROSS-TENANT ANALYTICS ANONYMISATION — 'ABSENCE IS THE CONTROL' IDIOM STATED EXPLICITLY. MOD-SA-17 lists a control 'No undo, restore or de-anonymise control (absence is the control)' with effect 'Anonymisation has no reversibility affordance for any role'. The root may_not 'Reverse an anonymisation' or 'De-anonymise a comparative view'.

CROSS-TENANT ANALYTICS ANONYMISATION — NO THRESHOLD IS STATED. No line in the extract gives a k-anonymity value, minimum cohort size, suppression rule for small cells, or any numeric anonymity parameter. The invariant is stated qualitatively only. Implementers must treat the anonymity criterion as unspecified.
findings.bindingOn: Implementation team — unstated parameter under a locked invariant

findings.claim: ONE-TRANSACTION AUDIT GUARANTEE — WHAT IT FORBIDS. Any change committing without its audit event in the same transaction. Canonical form: 'An administrative or operational change and its audit event commit in the same transaction, so an action that cannot be audited does not happen.' AC-SA-18-01 makes it structural: 'No code path exists where an administrative change commits and its audit event does not — the one-transaction guarantee, rendered ENFORCED.'
findings.bindingOn: Every mutating function on every surface, without exception (L115526)

findings.claim: ONE-TRANSACTION AUDIT GUARANTEE — ENFORCED AT BUILD AND RUNTIME. AC-30D-201: 'Every mutating application programming interface path writes an audit event in the same transaction; a mutating path with no audit write fails the build', enforcement point 'build assertion + runtime wrapper'. FB-COV-01 covers bypass: the runtime one-transaction wrapper refuses the write path; a path covered by neither is disabled by feature control on discovery and its changes reconstructed as an explicitly-marked retrospective audit class, 'never as original'.
findings.bindingOn: All mutating API paths; build pipeline

findings.claim: ONE-TRANSACTION AUDIT GUARANTEE — WHAT HAPPENS ON FAILURE. FB-SA-03: audit write failure → retry the whole transaction → refuse the action → terminal safe state 'The action does not happen'; recovery is 'Operator is told the action was refused and why; nothing to reconcile because nothing changed'. AC-4821: an audit-write failure 'never causes the audit record to be queued or dropped'. FB-AUDIT-TRANSACTION: 'The action does not happen and the user sees the failure', criticality Critical.
findings.bindingOn: SURF-SA all modules; every mutating function on every surface

findings.claim: ONE-TRANSACTION AUDIT GUARANTEE — AN AUDIT OUTAGE HALTS THE PLATFORM. 'An audit-store outage stops every server-side mutating action for every tenant and every account including the root.' The root explicitly may_not 'commit a server-side mutating action when the audit store is unavailable'. FB-SURFA-01: the four online surfaces refuse; only the Frontline has an alternative, a local durable append-only queue that accepts the audit event alongside the business event, and if the queue cannot accept, the device blocks the action.
findings.bindingOn: All five surfaces; every account including root

findings.claim: ONE-TRANSACTION AUDIT GUARANTEE — COMMISSIONING DEPENDS ON IT. FB-SEQ-001: if the audit store is unavailable at the moment of root creation the guarantee cannot be satisfied, so the platform 'remains STATE-PLAT-UNCOMMISSIONED and unreachable'. The invariant gates the platform's own existence, not merely its operations. Related: 'A tenant workspace never exists without an open tenant audit log; a workspace without a log is never allowed to exist, not even briefly.'

ONE-TRANSACTION AUDIT GUARANTEE — IMMUTABILITY IS RENDERED AS ABSENCE. The MOD-SA-18 audit search control set has 'no edit or delete affordance anywhere, not even greyed'. The root may_not 'Edit or delete an audit entry' or 'Suppress an event class'. No surface and no role can mutate the audit log; it is append-only, one log per tenant plus the platform log, and 'never shorter-lived than the data it evidences'.
findings.bindingOn: MOD-SA-18 Platform Audit / SCR-SA-25; all roles including root

findings.claim: ONE-TRANSACTION AUDIT GUARANTEE — RELEASE-BLOCKING. 'A failure in the one-transaction, append-only, or tenant-isolation groups blocks release unconditionally' — three release-blocking audit test groups. Separately, audit availability is validation dimension VD-30, the last of thirty-one and the one that 'stands alone' outside the four dimension bands.

ONE-TRANSACTION AUDIT GUARANTEE — EXTENDS TO NON-HUMAN IDENTITIES. 'Every action a non-human identity takes commits with its audit event in the same transaction.' AI rule two: AI 'may not delete, may not modify, may not cause an audit record not to be written'.
findings.bindingOn: All non-human/agent identities on every surface

findings.claim: TEST COVERAGE FOR THE INVARIANT LOCK. TEST-INV-001 is the named conformance test. One passage sizes it at seven attack routes per invariant and 42 expected refusals; another sizes it at twenty-four attempts across four console roles. See contradictions — implementers must pick a sizing with the client.

WHERE THE SIX RENDER — SCREEN INVENTORY. Platform Settings is the primary home (MOD-SA-07): SCR-SA-08 'Platform settings, ten categories' (CHK-013 numbering) / SCR-SA-08 'Platform Settings' (CHK-015 numbering); SCR-SA-SET-01 'Platform settings (six invariants render as locked controls)'; SCR-SA-SETTINGS 'The locked-invariant rendering' with storyboard SB-ARCH-008; an unnumbered screen 'Platform Settings, six invariants rendered locked'; SB-SA-07 carrying the ENFORCED-badge-with-lock-icon control. Two additional render sites: SB-SEC-006-S1 (Memory and Data locked rows — encryption and anonymisation) and SB-SEC-013-S1 'Super Admin Platform Overview and Health — security-posture panel listing the six ENFORCED invariants'.
findings.bindingOn: MOD-SA-07 Platform Settings; MOD-SA-01 Overview and Health

findings.claim: MOD-SA-07 IS THE OWNING MODULE, but its stated purpose and role list differ by chunk: 'renders six invariants locked with no off position' with roles Root+Admin (L2442); 'Band A: platform settings including six locked enforced invariants' with roles Root only (L11664); 'Configure platform-wide behaviour across ten categories … render the six enforced invariants as locked, hold the floor register, provide the emergency pause' with all four ROLE-PLAT-* (L44633); 'Platform settings including the six enforced invariants' with all four named roles (L60862); 'Orchestration controls, emergency pause, six enforced invariants, floor register' with roles empty (L116399). Key function identifiers also differ: FUNC-SA-INVARIANT-WRITE + FUNC-PLAT-BOUND-CHECK (L60862) vs FUNC-SA-INVARIANT-01 (L116399).
findings.bindingOn: Implementation team — module ownership is consistent, role scoping and function IDs are not

findings.claim: THE INVARIANTS DO NOT CONSTRAIN THE EMERGENCY PAUSE, AND VICE VERSA. Emergency pause is a critical-class action approved by the root, and pause and resume are separately approved. It 'never suppresses on-device gates, specification checks, severity classification, or the Severity 1 hold', renders as agent unavailability 'never silence', and no automatic resume exists. No line lets a pause suspend any of the six invariants.

THE CONSOLE IS NOT LOAD-BEARING FOR THE INVARIANTS. AC-SA-000-10: 'The console being wholly unavailable causes no change to deterministic on-device safety behaviour, agent enablement, or audit commitment on any tenant surface.' FB-SA-09 confirms: administration pauses, but 'runtime, deterministic safety, and audit continue'.
findings.bindingOn: SURF-SA control plane vs runtime separation

findings.claim: WORDING DRIFT — 'ENFORCED invariant' is applied to things OUTSIDE the closed six. Tenant/cross-tenant isolation is called 'an ENFORCED invariant' (AC-44A-18-1) and 'an enforced invariant' (FAIL-AI-35 recovery text), and the cross-tenant-boundary rule for non-human identities is labelled 'ENFORCED platform invariant, locked with no off position' — but the closed six contain cross-tenant analytics ANONYMISATION, a narrower thing, not isolation. Separately, on-device severity classification is catalogued as a control with effect 'Locked — on-device severity classification is platform-fixed with no off position' on SURF-DOH. Reading any of these as a seventh invariant would over-claim; reading the phrase 'ENFORCED invariant' as always meaning one of the six would under-claim.
findings.bindingOn: Implementation team — terminology hazard across module screens

findings.claim: NAMING ANOMALY IN THE EVAL HARNESS MODULE. MOD-SA-05's key_functions list at L21082 contains the identifier 'FEAT-SA-EVAL-GATE-OFF' on the same line whose purpose text reads 'the gate has no off position'. This identifier appears nowhere in the identifier index (which carries FEAT-SA-05-01/02/03 and FEAT-SA-0501..0503 for this module). Treat it as an unresolved artefact and confirm before building anything named for it.

A RELATED-BUT-DIFFERENT CLOSED SET EXISTS AND IS EASILY CONFLATED. The 'seven platform-fixed items' (L12100) are: specification gates; the evaluation gate; Severity 1's minimum action bundle; on-device severity classification; evidence immutability; cross-tenant data isolation; audit completeness. Only the evaluation gate is a literal member of both sets. Sandbox-before-publish, encryption at rest and encryption in transit appear in NEITHER of the seven. Do not merge the two lists.

THE FLOOR REGISTER IS A SEPARATE MECHANISM WITH A DIFFERENT FAILURE MODE. The eight-row platform floor register 'rejects rather than logs': a looser-than-floor value fails at the point of entry with the bound stated and is never stored. Contrast the invariants, where the attempt IS recorded (as a locked-setting-attempt). Implementers must not use one mechanism's behaviour for the other. FB-SA-10 and FB-FLOOR-001 cover an unavailable bound check: reject the write with the bound stated, existing value unchanged.
findings.bindingOn: MOD-SA-19 Tenant-Configuration Registry (single enforcement point); SCR-SA-10/SCR-SA-26

findings.claim: THE ROOT ACCOUNT SHAPE THE INVARIANTS BOUND. Exactly one Root Super Admin account exists for the life of the platform; it is backend-created at commissioning and 'not creatable through any user interface'; custody rests with the client; a second root cannot be created; the account may not be shared as a convenience login; and every root action is audited like any other. DEC-BREAKGLASS-001 (root break-glass procedure) is open at launch-readiness status.

closedSets.name: ENFORCED platform invariants
Platform-fixed items configurable at no value (SEVEN — a DIFFERENT set, do not merge with the six)
Platform floor register rows (EIGHT floor-and-ceiling rows; rejects rather than logs)
members: 8 rows stated as a count; the source does not enumerate all eight members in any single passage in the extract
named examples include the record-finish window (24h floor / 7d ceiling, contested under DEC-FINISH-001)
Severity 1 action bundle (add only, never remove)
genealogy depth (one level plus rework history)

closedSets.name: Critical-class actions requiring Root Super Admin approval (TEN as stated)
Named platform access classes into record-level tenant content (THREE and only three; no ambient browsing anywhere)
members: the normal support session (read-only without exception)

Layer 2 — comparative cross-tenant analytics: anonymised aggregates, enforced as an invariant
Layer 3 — record-level operational content: only through a named, audited, session-scoped access class

Effective-control evaluation order (FOURTEEN steps; 'Platform invariant' is step 1)
Authorization decision gauntlet (TWELVE steps, fixed order; step 11 is the one-transaction commit)

read current object state from the record of truth
commit action and audit in one transaction
enqueue device commands with honest states

closedSets.name: SURF-SA screen inventory as given in CHK-013 (TWENTY-SIX screens, SCR-SA-01..26; contradicted by a 22-screen list — see contradictions)
members: SCR-SA-07 Trace inspection (backend tooling at V1, not a screen)
SCR-SA-12 Console users and roles matrix
SCR-SA-16 Tenant metrics and anonymised comparative analytics
SCR-SA-19 Fleet view and device detail
SCR-SA-22 Compliance-emergency initiation and post-session report
SCR-SA-25 Platform audit search and export

contradictions: TEST-INV-001 SIZING. L111414 + L111416 size the invariant-lock conformance test at seven attack routes per invariant and '42 expected refusals (six invariants by seven routes)'. L117560 sizes the same named test at 'twenty-four attempts across four console roles' (6 x 4). Neither passage reconciles routes with roles. Both readings recorded; the implementation team must settle the test matrix with the client before writing TEST-INV-001.

UI IDIOM FOR 'LOCKED' — DISABLED CONTROL vs ABSENCE OF CONTROL. L60704 renders the six 'locked and unpressable' and L44041 renders an 'ENFORCED badge with lock icon' — both imply a present-but-inert control. L87376 states the opposite for the evaluation gate: allowed_roles 'none — it must render as an absence of control, not a disabled control'. L46121 takes the absence position for the audit log ('no edit or delete affordance anywhere, not even greyed'), L65361 takes it for enablement ('the enablement control is not offered at all while a scenario fails'), and L97560 takes it for anonymisation ('absence is the control'). L47849 (no off control, no approval path, no configuration key on any screen) also reads as absence. This is a direct visual-design conflict affecting every module screen. Both recorded.

ROOT AUTHORITY — 'UNRESTRICTED' vs BOUND. L14322 records the source describing the root as having 'unrestricted access to both bands' and then immediately constraining it with the six invariants, the evaluation gate and the three named access classes. Echoed by L44711 ('Everything, both bands' / 'gated by nothing except the platform invariants') and L87401 ('unrestricted console access' alongside may_not bypass the gate). The invariant clauses are the more specific and more frequently restated; both readings recorded.

ROOT AS SOLE CRITICAL-CLASS APPROVER vs CREATOR-IS-NEVER-APPROVER. L21146 (DEC-ROOTSOD-001): §8.8.1/§8.8.3 make the root the sole approver of the critical class 'gated by nothing but the invariants', while §3.5, §4.5.2 and §5.11.1 make creator-is-never-approver absolute. Unresolved; affects whether the root can approve a critical-class action it initiated.

PLATFORM AUDIT NAMED EVENT CLASS COUNT — THREE VALUES. 20 classes (L46178, AC-SA-18-03 / TEST-SA-18-N1 'Record all twenty named classes'), 21 classes (L4629), 22 classes (L47835 FEAT-SA-1802 / SUB-SA-1802, and L48838 'twenty-two … including attempts on locked settings'). L47835 records the 20-vs-22 conflict explicitly. This matters directly: the locked-setting-attempt class is a member of whichever list is authoritative.

SANDBOX-BEFORE-PUBLISH — GATE vs ENVIRONMENT. L108063 (DEC-DEPLOY-001): sandbox-before-publish is an enforced invariant per §8.7.4, yet 'no environment inventory is specified anywhere' and the word 'environment' appears once, as a setting (L108105). Reading the invariant as a staging-environment commitment would be an over-claim; reading it as merely a queue check may be an under-claim. Unresolved.

AUDIT IMMUTABILITY vs TAMPER-EVIDENCE. L118587 (DEC-AUDIT-001, L117780): the source promises an immutable append-only audit log under the one-transaction guarantee while listing tamper-evident audit chains among items explicitly out of V1. RISK-SEC-11 (L105069) states the consequence plainly — suppression beneath the application is not detectable by the platform at V1. The invariant holds at the application layer only.

OFFLINE HONOURING OF THE ONE-TRANSACTION GUARANTEE. L74372 (DEC-AUDITOFF-001): the Statement of Work does not state how the guarantee is honoured on a device that cannot reach the server; the two alternatives ('a device that silently records unaudited work', 'a device that cannot work offline') both contradict stated positions. The adopted working position — a local durable append-only queue committing business and audit events together at device scope, blocking the action when the queue cannot preserve it — is a Derived Clarification awaiting a client decision on its bounds, not a source fact.

ERASURE vs AUDIT IMMUTABILITY. L97689 (DEC-ERASEAUD-001): audit immutability and right-to-erasure structurally conflict; three options are on the table (audit rows never altered; audit rows undergo identity replacement; identity replaced plus a tombstone). Rule five treats option (b) as the working interpretation while the recommendation is option (c). Open.

SCR-SA SCREEN NUMBERING — TWO INCOMPATIBLE SCHEMES. L42793–L42818 gives 26 screens where SCR-SA-08 = 'Platform settings, ten categories' and SCR-SA-10 = 'Platform floor register'. L48730–L48751 gives 22 screens where SCR-SA-08 = 'Platform Settings' but SCR-SA-10 = 'Approval queue' (and SCR-SA-01 = 'Console sign-in', absent from the first list). Both agree that Platform Settings is SCR-SA-08; everything else diverges. The control 'Approve anything touching the six enforced invariants' is anchored to SCR-SA-10 at L48793, which resolves to the Approval queue only under the second scheme.

MOD-SA-05 KEY FUNCTION 'FEAT-SA-EVAL-GATE-OFF' (L21082) sits on the same line as the module purpose 'the gate has no off position' (L21082), and contradicts every statement of the evaluation-gate invariant. The identifier is absent from the identifier index. Recorded as an unresolved artefact rather than a feature.

ENCRYPTION INVARIANTS LOCKED BUT MECHANISM UNDECIDED. L104032 renders encryption at rest and in transit as locked with no control and no approval path, while DEC-SEC-014 (L103926) leaves key hierarchy, custody, rotation and customer-managed keys open with 'no value proposed for rotation periods'. L107079 additionally records that key management and artifact signing carry two conflicting priorities at once ('2 by consequence', '10 by visibility'). Not a logical contradiction in the invariant, but a locked control with no defined substance.

'ENFORCED INVARIANT' USED FOR NON-MEMBERS. Tenant/cross-tenant isolation is called an ENFORCED invariant at L94296 and L90384, and the non-human cross-tenant-boundary rule is called an 'ENFORCED platform invariant, locked with no off position' at L18107 — but the closed six contain cross-tenant analytics ANONYMISATION, not isolation. On-device severity classification is separately catalogued as 'Locked — platform-fixed with no off position' on SURF-DOH (L61487). Either these are additional invariants (contradicting the count of six, restated 15+ times) or the phrase is used loosely. Both readings recorded; the count-of-six evidence is far stronger.

CRITICAL-CLASS ENUMERATION COUNT. L55942 records the source stating ten named critical actions while 'the enumeration as written lists eleven items with pause and resume named separately'. Affects the approval-authority table the invariant screens sit beside.

MOD-SA-07 CATEGORY COUNT vs ACCEPTANCE-CRITERIA GROUPS. The module and its screen are described as 'ten categories' (L44633, L42800), while the acceptance criteria for the same module run AC-SA-07-01-xx through AC-SA-07-15-xx — fifteen numbered sub-groups (identifier index: L44051 through L44627). The invariants render inside this module, so the category structure is load-bearing for placement. Unresolved.

MOD-SA-07 ROLE SCOPING. Roles allowed on the Platform Settings module are given as Root+Admin (L2442), Root Super Admin only (L11664), all four ROLE-PLAT-* (L44633), all four named roles (L60862), and empty (L116399). Since this is the screen that renders the locked invariants, who can even open it is unsettled — though every passage agrees none of them can change an invariant.

value.topic: SURF-SA cross-cutting spine: tenant lifecycle, commercial tier model, and data lifecycle/archival (MOD-SA-09, MOD-SA-11, MOD-SA-17)

findings.claim: MOD-SA-09 'Tenants, Lifecycle and Pilots' is the owning module: tenant list, invitation-driven onboarding, three-state suspension machine, tier change and pending downgrade, pilots, groups, and an eight-tab tenant detail page; classified SoW Fact §8.9.1–§8.9.6, with 14 key functions FUNC-SA-09-01-A1 … FUNC-SA-09-06-A2.

OBJ-SA-TENANT is authoritatively owned by SURF-SA and enumerates EIGHT states: invited, pilot, active, soft, hard, compliance, pending downgrade, archived. Related objects: OBJ-SA-TENANTSTATE (tenant state history), OBJ-SA-PILOT, OBJ-SA-GROUP, OBJ-SA-TIER, OBJ-SA-REGISTRY. The source does NOT declare this enumeration closed anywhere, and no member count is asserted.

There is NO reconciled legal-transition table for the tenant lifecycle anywhere in the extract. DEC-SUSP-002 ('the relationship between tenant block, soft, hard, compliance suspension and archival') is OPEN, recommendation Option A 'one lifecycle', explicitly recorded as 'Blocking for Super Admin module 9's state model'. DEC-SUSP-003 ('which suspension-state transitions are valid') is OPEN, recommendation Option C 'escalation free, de-escalation governed, expressed as an enumerated table' — and that table does not exist in the source. Implementers must not synthesise one.

findings.claim: The 'invited' state is orphaned: it appears only in the OBJ-SA-TENANT enumeration (L45003/45004). Every named onboarding/provisioning sub-machine in the source uses different state names and none contains 'invited' — SafeDraft/Provisioning/Seeded/AwaitingAcceptance/Active/HandedOff/ProvisioningFailed (L75159); Requested/Provisioning/Active/ProvisioningFailed/Onboarded (L52415); Intent/Validating/Qualified/Blocked/SafeState/Provisioning (L66938). The mapping from 'invited' to any of these is not stated.

Tenant creation is invitation-driven only: AC-SA-09-01 'No public self-signup path exists; every tenant is created by the client's platform team' (hard gate). Restated: pilots are invitation-only with no public free trial (L66828, L75096). AC-SA-09-02 makes tenant isolation architectural, not a permission setting (hard gate).

A partially validated tenant must never become active; the record stays in a safe draft state where no user can authenticate, no operational data can be created, no device can enroll and no work package can be generated (hard gate). AC-WF-TEN-001-01: 'No tenant becomes reachable before its isolated data space is confirmed provisioned.' Provisioning rollback is explicit and non-destructive — the record is returned to safe draft and is NEVER deleted, because nothing on the platform is purged. Onboarding is enumerated at six provisioning steps.

Exactly one Tenant Admin is seeded per tenant by the platform side (AC-WF-TEN-002-01); thereafter user management is tenant-administered. Activation-record lifetime and the invited-not-activated stale threshold are UNSPECIFIED — DEC-INVITE-001 is TBD/Client Decision Required, with the noted impact that 'an activation link with no expiry is a standing credential-issuance path'.

OBJ-SA-PILOT states are active pilot, converted, extended, expired. Pilot term is 60 days default, extendable to 90 at the client's discretion. AC-SA-09-11: pilot conversion preserves the tenant identifier and requires no re-onboarding (hard gate). A pilot tenant is functionally identical to a paying tenant — same platform, same gates, same isolation.

Pilot expiry NEVER acts by itself: SCHED-PILOT-EXPIRY's terminal states are 'the pilot continues operating; overdue state visible and escalating' and, separately, 'converted, extended or ended' by a person. This aligns with the standing rule that a timeout is never a decision.

Suspension escalation triggers are commercial defaults, both configurable by the client's platform team: soft at 30 days of non-payment, hard at 60 days of non-payment (or commercial action by the client's team). Scheduled definitions SCHED-SUSPEND-SOFT and SCHED-SUSPEND-HARD carry them.

SOFT suspension semantics (hard gate): blocks master-data writes while runs continue to be created, scheduled and executed (AC-SA-09-03). Blocks creation of new Jobs, Workers, locations, shifts, parts and ALL configuration edits, while recertification of existing workers deliberately stays open. Only the Tenant Admin sees a banner; no other tenant user sees any indication (AC-SA-09-04). No worker-facing message appears. The banner has no Dismiss control while the state persists.
findings.bindingOn: all nine roles; every DOH/STU/CC write path

findings.claim: HARD suspension semantics (hard gate): read-only except the enumerated completion pipeline — no new runs, while in-flight runs complete, capture, sync, compute summaries and close, with mandatory notifications and audit continuing (AC-SA-09-05; AC-RBAC-404 places the suspension check BEFORE the role grant). The source names it 'the enumerated completion pipeline' but never states a member count, so the pipeline must not be treated as a closed set.
findings.bindingOn: all nine roles; authorisation layer ordering

findings.claim: COMPLIANCE suspension semantics (hard gate): blocks ALL logins immediately for every tenant role on every web surface, stops in-flight runs, and locks devices at next contact with the fixed message (AC-SA-09-06). AC-SA-09-08: the ONLY platform-side entry into a compliance-suspended tenant is the dual-authorised compliance-emergency path (root + one Admin). Compliance suspension is one of the ten critical-class actions requiring root approval.
findings.bindingOn: all nine roles; support access machinery

findings.claim: Per-role behaviour under the suspension states, as the source states it. Supervisor: create run allowed under Active and Soft, prohibited under Hard and Compliance; create Job and create worker record prohibited under Soft, Hard and Compliance; recertification of an existing worker allowed under Active and Soft. Worker: execute in-flight run allowed under Active and Soft, allowed with conditions under Hard (completion pipeline only), prohibited under Compliance; start a new run prohibited under Hard and Compliance; workers see nothing on mobile in Soft or Hard. Quality Manager: review a summary and close a record allowed under Active, Soft and Hard, prohibited under Compliance; release a lot hold allowed with conditions under Hard where it belongs to the completion pipeline, prohibited under Compliance. Tenant Admin: edit a tenant setting prohibited under Soft, Hard and Compliance. Any role: log in prohibited under Compliance.
findings.bindingOn: Supervisor, Worker, Quality Manager, Tenant Admin, all tenant roles

findings.claim: The Read-only Auditor's suspension-state cells are NOT stated. The source's suspension role table covers Supervisor, Worker, Quality Manager, Tenant Admin and 'any role' for login only; no row states what a Read-only Auditor may read under soft or hard suspension. This is a genuine silence, not an omission of the extract.
findings.bindingOn: ROLE-TEN-AUD under suspension — Client Decision Required

findings.claim: Console-role authority to cause tenant-state transitions. Platform Admin (ROLE-PLAT-ADMIN) may create a tenant record, assign tier, seed the first Tenant Admin, provision the implementation authoring role, APPLY SOFT AND HARD SUSPENSION, LIFT A SUSPENSION, suspend a device, and raise a wipe request; may not self-approve a critical-class action, may not approve a wipe (root-only), may not apply compliance suspension without root approval. Hard suspension requires a typed confirmation and reason class. The compliance-suspension control 'opens a critical-class request rather than acting' (Admin drafts, Root Super Admin approves). Platform Engineer (ROLE-PLAT-ENG) may NOT create a tenant record or raise/approve a wipe. Support (ROLE-PLAT-SUP) is read-only with session-scoped elevation only and may not create a tenant.

Tenant-role authority over lifecycle is uniformly nil except two read/request affordances. Tenant Admin may view own tier, entitlements, caps and consumption (read-only), request a self-service tier upgrade (effective immediately), request a downgrade (request only), see the suspension banner in soft or hard, and read tenant_state_history through the audit log; may NOT execute a downgrade, change a suspension state, change ladder thresholds, or view tenant-group membership. Supervisor may not request an upgrade or downgrade, may not change suspension state or ladder thresholds, and the tier/entitlement/caps/consumption view is Unavailable to them. Worker sees only the fixed compliance message on the device.

Every tenant-state transition writes tenant_state_history and is audited; the history is compared against per-device applied state in reconciliation. OBJ-SA-TENANTSTATE relates the tenant to the platform audit log. Tenant lifecycle state changes are Band B routine Admin work EXCEPT compliance suspension, which is critical class.

Suspension enforcement is never a notification and never a UI state. AC-SA-09-unnumbered: 'None of the notifications enforces the suspension; the suspension is enforced by the authorisation layer and, on devices, by the applied command.' Invariant: a notification is never the sole mechanism enforcing a hold, qualification, authorisation, approval, suspension or device command.

Device-side honesty rules bound how suspension is rendered. AC-SA-09-10: a device lock is never rendered as applied before the device acknowledges it. FB-TEN-01: where the command channel cannot deliver, the tenant's central state is authoritative and every server-side action is refused, but no surface may display that device as suspended. FB-SUSP-001: unreached devices are individually listed as unreached. On reconnection DEC-SYNC-001 (adopted Option C, ratification outstanding) orders phase 1 stop-class commands — suspension in all three states, de-authorisation, wipe, compliance stop — before the full capture upload, then enabling-class commands.

Cached suspension state on a device is trusted only within the tenant-set credential-trust window, default approximately 24 hours with a platform ceiling of 72 hours; beyond it the device blocks new work rather than trusting stale authority. FB-PLT-004's fallback for an undeliverable suspension is precisely to rely on cache-validity expiry.

AC-SA-09-14 (hard gate): 'No operational action of any kind can be taken from the tenant detail page by any console role — visibility, not intervention.' Reinforced by the sixteen prohibited acts binding all four console roles including the root, and by the invariant that no ambient browsing exists anywhere on the console.
findings.bindingOn: all four platform console roles including ROLE-PLAT-ROOT

findings.claim: AC-SA-09-13 (hard gate): tenant groups have no operational behaviour and are never visible in any tenant surface — OBJ-SA-GROUP is 'an internal label only'.
Tier bands are three, gated by Worker-Shifts per month: Starter below 100, Growth 100 to 199, Enterprise 200 and above. The allocation period is monthly. Active Locations meter at Site level only.

Worker-Shift definition (hard gates): AC-GOAL-060 'a worker attached to work in one calendar shift meters exactly one Worker-Shift regardless of run count'; AC-GOAL-061 'where a substitution occurs, each worker who actually performed work meters one'; AC-B11-7 restates attribution as exactly once per worker per calendar shift. The source's own worked example: one shift with a substitution meters 2 Worker-Shifts.

OBJ-SA-TIER (Tier record) lifecycle is four states: draft, pending root approval, published, superseded. Two other renderings in the frozen source are shorter — draft/published (L10411, L56912) and 'version created/published' (L21282) — and one gives only 'versioned/approvable' (L2195). The four-state form is the fullest and is the one the SURF-SA object cards carry.

AC-SA-11-01 (hard gate): tier records carry all six field groups and NO price metadata; the platform does not price or bill. The six field groups named elsewhere are entitlement flags, limits and caps, threshold defaults, effective dates, the grandfathering rule, and the approval reference. Price metadata on a tier record is Explicitly prohibited; pricing, invoicing and payment sit entirely outside the platform. There is no payment integration anywhere, so no validation may depend on a payment event.

AC-SA-11-02 (hard gate): tier publication is critical-class and cannot be performed by an Admin alone. Tier publication is member 1 of the ten critical-class actions requiring root approval. The Admin may draft a tier version and may not publish one; the Platform Engineer may neither draft nor publish. Workflow 23.11: Admin drafts, Root Super Admin approves, published with its audit event in one transaction.

AC-SA-11-03 (hard gate): grandfathering treatment is MANDATORY in the change record before submission; the control 'mandatory grandfathering declaration' must be completed before tier submission is possible. Tenant treatment on publication is a two-member vocabulary: grandfathered or migrated. Workflow 23.11's terminal state is 'tenants grandfathered or migrated per the declared treatment'. The source does not state any default treatment, any per-tenant selection mechanism, or what happens to a tenant whose current consumption no longer fits the republished band — all three are silences.
findings.bindingOn: MOD-SA-11 publication; every tenant referencing the superseded version

findings.claim: AC-SA-11-04 (hard gate): per-tenant overrides are flags on the tenant record (OBJ-SA-OVERRIDE) and NEVER edits to the tier. Precedence between an override and the tier entitlement is UNRESOLVED — DEC-FEAT-004 is open with recommendation 'the override may restrict freely and may grant only where an explicit tenant entitlement exists'. A separate absolute holds regardless: a global disable is a ceiling and cannot be re-enabled by any tier, entitlement, override, cohort or tenant value (AC-SA-20-2-03).

Entitlement gating stated: AC-SA-11-06 'Agent Author gates Growth and Enterprise; Job Type and Service Type are ungated', enforced at Studio Agent Builder gating read from the tier record. Composing action agents is Explicitly prohibited at launch and the Agent Author capability is Unavailable on Starter.

Caps do not stop work. The usage ladder is four rungs of the monthly allocation: 80 per cent in-product banner rendered tenant-side; 100 per cent escalation notification; 100 to 125 per cent burst-tolerance band within which the floor keeps running, with a burst-entry event raised at crossing; above 125 per cent a flag opening the client's commercial conversation, never enforcement. The named failure path is explicit: 'the platform does not stop the floor at a threshold'. Thresholds are per-tenant defaults tunable in the Super Admin platform console.
findings.bindingOn: MOD-SA-11 caps, MOD-SA-12 ladder, MOD-DOH-01 tenant view

findings.claim: Upgrade is tenant self-service and immediate; consumption is NEVER reset on a tier change. Worked example: 80 Worker-Shifts consumed of a 100 Starter ceiling becomes 80 of 199 on Growth. Recovery from a cap breach is 'tier upgrade, effective immediately with consumption carried forward'.

Downgrade never takes effect mid-cycle. AC-SA-09-12 (hard gate): 'Downgrades never execute mid-cycle and carry a visible pending-downgrade status, queued behind consumption fit.' AC-GOAL-066 restates it. The mechanism: a downgrade whose target ceiling sits below current consumption does not fail and does not truncate; it queues, is labelled pending downgrade, and takes effect at the start of the FIRST CYCLE IN WHICH CONSUMPTION FITS. The stated rationale is arithmetic on the monthly allocation period, not a separate rule — consumption already booked in the current cycle would exceed the lower ceiling, and the platform truncates nothing. The tenant requests; the client's platform team executes. A later tier change supersedes a queued downgrade, recorded.
findings.bindingOn: MOD-SA-09 tier change; MOD-DOH-01 request path

findings.claim: Automatic tier downgrade is PERMANENTLY REJECTED (proposal P12), alongside automatic suspension release on payment (P13), gate timeout becoming a decision (P14) and automatic device wipe on prolonged offline (P16) — four of sixteen assessed proposals P1–P16 are Explicitly prohibited or rejected.
findings.bindingOn: MOD-SA-09, MOD-SA-11 — no scheduler may execute a downgrade or a release

findings.claim: When no published tier fits a tenant at onboarding, FB-SEQ-003 governs: assign the nearest published tier and record a per-tenant override flag; if no published tier fits and the override would breach a floor, the onboarding request stays qualified but UNPROVISIONED and no data space is created. Recovery is an Admin drafting the tier version and the root publishing it as a critical-class action with its grandfathering treatment declared.

Metering that feeds the caps is event-sourced across five dimensions — worker-shift, agent-run, tokens by router role, storage, seat or device — with four storage dimensions metered (evidence media, workflow packages, the parts registry, training content). A metering change is reprocessing, not data loss: the ledger is reconstructable end to end (hard gate). Ledger export to the client's commercial systems is Root Super Admin / Admin only and is itself audited.

Per-role account ceilings are UNSPECIFIED. DEC-SEAT-001 is open: 'What per-role account ceilings apply, given the commercial model meters Worker-Shifts and not seats?' with options (a) no ceilings, (b) a soft advisory threshold, (c) hard per-role caps carried in the tier record; recommendation is (b) for Tenant Admin and Quality Manager only. No seat cap may be implemented from the tier record until this lands.

AC-SA-17-01 (hard gate): 'No purge capability exists anywhere on the platform for any account; nothing ages out of existence.' AC-GOAL-014: 'No record is deleted by age under any configuration.' AC-LIFE-001: every retention row resolves to tiering, supersession, anonymisation, or the named-standard exception. Tombstones mark de-registration and de-authorisation, never data destruction. Under the no-purge model storage accumulates perpetually; the tiering curve is the cost lever and there is no delete lever at all. The 'Delete tenant data' control DOES NOT EXIST on the archival screen.

AC-SA-17-02 (hard gate): the retention value is a HOT-RETRIEVABILITY HORIZON, default fifteen years, and shortening it MOVES data rather than deleting it. Beyond the horizon data tiers to lower-cost storage and remains retrievable. Retention is uniform across tiers — never tier-gated. Retention-value changes are critical-class, ride maker-checker with root approval, and write to both the platform and the tenant audit trails; the value is configurable only within platform floor-register bounds and an out-of-bound value is REJECTED at entry with the bound stated, never clamped.

The tenant closure sequence is five states: Active → ExportProvided → Archived → Anonymised → Tiered. Storyboard SB-030's terminal states are 'Tenant archived', 'Anonymised at 24 months', 'Tiered beyond the hot-retrievability horizon and still retrievable'. Two longer machines cover the same ground and do not contradict it but are not reconciled to it: the offboarding machine SEQ-032 (11 states, HardSuspended → … → FinalState) and the final lifecycle machine SEQ-033 (8 states, Archived → … → Settled).

AC-SA-17-09 (hard gate): offboarding executes export-on-archival AT NO CHARGE before archival. The 'Skip the export' control is Disabled. 'Approve archival' is Root Super Admin only and its effect is that the workspace becomes unusable and wholly retained. Restore and erasure controls are critical-class with Root Super Admin approving and Admin executing. If the export cannot complete for volume, archival does not proceed — the tenant remains hard suspended, data intact and audit continuing; if the earlier root approval has aged, archival is re-approved.

Archival is REVERSIBLE inside stated windows and the windows are three: free within 6 months; engineering-time fee between 6 and 12 months; beyond 12 months a fresh tenancy, with historical data remaining exportable for a retrieval fee. The branch vocabulary is ReactivatedFree / ReactivatedFee / FreshTenantOnly.

ANONYMISATION IS THE ONE IRREVERSIBLE ACT ON THE PLATFORM. AC-SA-17-05: runs at 24 months for standard commercial tenants and NEVER in Regulated-Industry mode (hard gate; AC-SCHED-342 enforces the mode assertion in the handler). AC-SA-17-06: preserves the measurement, the result and the evidence and replaces only the identity; it severs identity RESOLUTION and never rewrites audit rows. AC-SA-17-07: cannot be reversed by any account, and switching into Regulated-Industry mode later does not resurrect identities. AC-SA-17-08: upcoming anonymisation events are surfaced before they execute. The 'Reverse anonymisation' control does not exist, now or later; the Root Super Admin explicitly may not reverse an anonymisation, may not de-anonymise a comparative view, and may not trigger worker anonymisation manually. SB-SCHED-23's stated terminal position: 'there is no terminal safe state that restores the identity; the safe state is prevention.'
findings.bindingOn: all nine roles including ROLE-PLAT-ROOT; MOD-SA-17

findings.claim: AC-SA-17-04 (hard gate): a legal hold (OBJ-SA-LEGALHOLD, states placed / in force / released) suspends TIERING and COMPLIANCE-DRIVEN DELETION for its named scope; place and release are both dual-approved critical-class and tenant-visible. AC-SCHED-340: zero transitions occur inside a legal-hold scope. Legal-hold placement failure is the gravest case in MOD-SA-17 — immediate escalation rather than a silent retry, with tiering suspended for the intended scope by a broader manual hold until the precise one can be placed.

The right-to-erasure workflow is FIVE steps — request, scope, legal-hold check, execution, erasure certificate. AC-SA-17-11 (hard gate): the workflow cannot skip the legal-hold check and always writes a certificate to both audit trails. The console control is a 'five-step guided right-to-erasure sequence' with Admin drafting and Root Super Admin approving. Deletion occurs ONLY where a named compliance standard requires it, and the list of those standards is owed by the client (DEC-DELETE-001, open — 'the no-purge model's single dependency'). Until it lands, no deletion path is built or promised.

Lifecycle scheduler failure always fails SAFE toward retention. FB-LIFE-001: data stays hot, 'which costs storage and risks nothing, because nothing is purged'. FB-SA-08: for tiering, data stays hot — costs money, loses nothing; the anonymisation backfill must be idempotent and must verify before acting. FB-SEQ-033: a failed tiering run leaves data in hot storage, a failed anonymisation leaves identities in place — neither failure can delete anything. The data-lifecycle scheduler identity is narrowed to one tenant per occurrence so a defect cannot cross tenants.

Data-lifecycle READ authority: MOD-SA-17's roles_allowed include Root Super Admin, Admin, Platform Engineer, Support, Tenant Admin (read-only) and Read-only Auditor (read-only). The Read-only Auditor may read retention posture, holds and schedules for its own tenant, and may NOT trigger or suppress anonymisation, execute archival or erasure, or purge data. The Tenant Admin may not write the retention horizon, the Regulated-Industry toggle or feature enablement, and may not place or release a legal hold.

Data-lifecycle screen SCR-SA-24 has five areas — Retention, Tiering, Legal hold, Anonymisation, Archival — and the module's purpose requires every upcoming lifecycle event to be surfaced BEFORE it runs. Additional SURF-SA lifecycle screens named: SCR-SA-LIFECYCLE, SCR-SA-DEVICEWIPE, SCR-SA-ARCHIVEDETAIL, SCR-SA-ARCHIVE-EXECUTE.

Root-account unavailability FREEZES the entire lifecycle spine: compliance suspension, device wipe, emergency pause/resume, retention changes, legal hold, severity-catalog and floor changes, and all account/role changes all stop, because critical-class approval is root-only and exactly one root account exists. DEC-ROOTSUCC-001 (how root custody is recovered) is open/TBD, and DEC-ROOTSOD-001 records that the root approving its own critical action sits directly against the platform's self-approval prohibition.

Nine roles is DERIVED, not SoW Fact: 5 tenant (ROLE-TEN-ADMIN, ROLE-TEN-SUP, ROLE-TEN-QM, ROLE-TEN-AUD, ROLE-TEN-WKR) + 4 platform console (ROLE-PLAT-ROOT with exactly one account, ROLE-PLAT-ADMIN, ROLE-PLAT-ENG, ROLE-PLAT-SUP). The source states five and four separately and never adds them; Appendix L classifies the combined figure as Derived arithmetic over §3.5 and §8.8.2. Authoring capacity is a GRANT layered on Supervisor/Quality Manager, never a tenth role.
